sentences.text: It can be included as part of the Science subject, alongside Physics, Chemistry and Biology.

sections.label: Water price increase and U-save
sections.summary: Despite U-save rebates, the water price increase involves all water consumption, including industries and businesses, not only domestic users.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Although the Government has provided additional assistance through U-save rebates, the increase in the price of water does not only comprise domestic users or consumption at home, but it also involves all aspects of water consumption like industries and businesses.

sections.label: Assurance on consumer price increases
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government can assure that consumers will not experience price increases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can the Government give an assurance that consumers will not experience price increases?

sections.label: Budget short-term and long-term needs
sections.summary: The Budget addresses short-term needs and assistance, but longer-term directions are needed on education, workforce, economic adaptability and social safety nets.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: In this Budget, it does address some short-term needs where assistance is provided to those in need and who may be temporarily unemployed and for our vulnerable groups.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: But more importantly, we must seek to have longer-term directions; where we must get our fundamentals right on diverse education pathways for our future generations, readiness of our workforce, adaptability to new variation in economic models and sustainable approach to our social safety net.

sections.label: R&D patents and business returns
sections.summary: Singapore invested in R&D, with 1,469 patents filed by residents in 2015, a 12.7% increase, but business returns lag.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: We have been investing in the past decade in R&D, creating more platforms to innovate.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: We have seen an increase in the number of innovative ideas, as evident by the 1,469 patents that were filed by Singaporean residents in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: That is a 12.7% year-on-year increase on the patents that are registered.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: But the corresponding number of ideas and patents from earlier batches that have borne tangible achievements, as in business returns, pales in comparison.

sections.label: Dementia care in Singapore
sections.summary: Dementia affects about 10% of seniors aged 60 and above, and the MP asks about the Yishun pilot trial.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: In Singapore, the prevalence of dementia is about 10% amongst seniors aged 60 and above.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: The number of seniors with dementia is set to rise, especially with a rapidly ageing population.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Countries like Japan and Taiwan have shown that dementia-friendly communities where PWDs living in their homes have resulted in lower cost to healthcare.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Therefore, it is imperative to raise awareness and put in place initiatives that support persons with dementia to age in place.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: I support this initiative and would like to ask the Ministry about the outcome of the first pilot trial of community-based dementia care efforts in Yishun.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: What are the lessons learnt from this trial and how long will it take to train resources to cope with the existing situation of 10% dementia patients?

sections.label: Workforce employability and long-term change
sections.summary: The passage states the need to help the existing workforce stay employable and asks whether to evolve a new culture or reinvent incrementally.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: In the short term, we have to address the needs to assist our existing workforce to make sure that they remain employable.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: But on the long run, we have to consider: do we take bolder measures to evolve a new culture or do we continue to move ahead to reinvent through incremental changes?

sections.label: Water price revision
sections.summary: The Government decided to revise the water price substantially to reflect water's true scarcity value.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The Government, therefore, decided to revise the water price substantially, to reflect water's true scarcity value.

sections.label: Water prices unchanged 17 years
sections.summary: Costs were kept down and water prices were held unchanged for 17 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: As a result, we have been able to keep our costs down, the cost of water, and hold water prices unchanged for 17 years.

sections.label: Three desalination plants
sections.summary: Three desalination plants are being built within the next three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Indeed, we are building three desalination plants within the next three years.

sections.label: Desalination first-year price increase
sections.summary: First-year desalination price rose from $0.78 per cubic metre at SingSpring to $1.08 at Marina East, a 40% increase.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Looking at the first year of desalination, for instance, while the first-year price for our first plant, SingSpring Desalination Plant, was $0.78 per cubic metre, the first-year price of our latest plant at Marina East was $1.08 per cubic metre, some 40% increase.

sections.label: Pipeline renewal rate increase
sections.summary: PUB must more than double old pipeline renewal from 20 to 50 kilometres per year to minimise leaks and disruptions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: As our pipelines age, PUB will have to more than double the rate of renewal of old pipelines from the current 20 kilometres per year to 50 kilometres per year to minimise pipe leaks and disruptions.

sections.label: Business water bill increases
sections.summary: 75% of businesses will see water bill increases of less than $25 per month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: For businesses, 75% will see an increase of less than $25 per month in their water bills.

sections.label: HDB household water bill changes
sections.summary: One- and 2-room HDB households face no increase; other HDB flats rise $2 to $11 monthly, with water at about 1% of household income.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: One- and 2-room HDB households will not experience any increase in their bills.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: For other HDB flat types, monthly water bills will go up by $2 to $11 per month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Overall, water will still be affordable because it will remain at about 1% of household income.

sections.label: Singapore water stress ranking
sections.summary: The World Resources Institute ranked Singapore first among countries with the greatest water stress risk in 2040.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Singapore was ranked first among countries with the greatest risk of water stress in 2040, according to the World Resources Institute.

sections.label: Figures for two periods
sections.summary: The figure was about $550 million between 2013 and 2015, and $339 million between 2010 and 2012.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Between 2013 and 2015, it was about $550 million and between 2010 and 2012, it was $339 million.

sections.label: NEWater versus desalination plant choice
sections.summary: Asks how PUB decides whether to build more NEWater plants instead of desalination plants, since NEWater is cheaper.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: How does PUB make that determination whether it should construct more NEWater plants, as opposed to desalination plants, because NEWater is obviously cheaper.

sections.label: Linggiu Reservoir failure and water tax
sections.summary: Asks whether a rise in water conservation tax can be anticipated if the Linggiu Reservoir fails.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With regard to the Linggiu Reservoir, assuming that it does fail, can we anticipate a rise in water conservation tax?

sections.label: Funding water infrastructure whole-of-Government
sections.summary: The Minister for Finance will be asked to look at a whole-of-Government approach to funding water infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: What we will do is I will ask the Minister for Finance to look at the whole-of-Government approach in funding our water infrastructure.

sections.label: Tipping point between NEWater and desalination
sections.summary: Reclaiming more used water makes processing harder and costlier, creating a tipping point between desalination and NEWater plants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: But as you reclaim more of this used water to be processed, the concentration, as I have mentioned to you, becomes even more difficult to process and, therefore, more costly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: There is a tipping point between when it is better to have a desalination plant, which is easier to convey the sea water to, and a NEWater plant where we have to convey the used water to.

sections.label: Water price as LRMC
sections.summary: The proposed water price increase is LRMC, the price of producing the next drop of water.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The price of water, as it stands today, that we have proposed to increase, is LRMC, which is the price of producing the next drop of water.

sections.label: 1997 water pricing and tariff revision
sections.summary: From 1997 water tariffs and structure were revised to reflect LRMC and make users know the price of what they use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: If I recall correctly, it was in 1997 when we decided to price water correctly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: At that time, it was not only not priced correctly, the structure of the tariff was also very difficult to encourage conservation, conserving of water, to charge water according to its value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: It was only in 1997 when we looked at really what we need to do to get that next drop of water, given the situation we were facing with our neighbours, given the expiry of the water agreement by 2060, that we consciously decided that we have to start thinking around how to make sure people understand the value of water.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: So, from 1997 onwards, we revised the water tariff and structure to reflect the cost of producing that water, LRMC, and, therefore, to make sure users know the price of what they use.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: By 1976, Kodak held more than 90% of film sales and 85% of camera sales in the US alone.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: By 2012, we recall how Kodak filed for Chapter 11 Bankruptcy.

sections.label: Mental health funding and programmes
sections.summary: Budget 2017 channels $160 million to the mental health fund and new programmes, including dementia-friendly communities, pleasing 10 Geylang Serai Taskforce organisations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Budget 2017 has presented ways to further strengthen the circle of treatment, counselling and the network for mental health, especially at the community level. $160 million will be channeled towards the mental health fund and new programmes and initiatives, including the dementia-friendly communities programme.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: With this increase in funding, all 10 organisations, which are part of my mental health Taskforce in Geylang Serai, are pleased with its announcement.

sections.label: Geylang Serai mental health dialogues
sections.summary: Geylang Serai holds open mental health dialogues, makes cross-over referrals to TCM at Sian Chay, and hosted the Asia Pacific Mental Wellness Conference where the Global Mental Health Alliance was launched.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In fact, in Geylang Serai, we always have open dialogues on mental health and sharing is done by people of all races.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We also implement cross-over referrals, which means that anyone who receives treatment and assistance from the Silver Support team, will also be directed to receive traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) treatment at Sian Chay Medical Association to learn how to use herbs, how to relax their minds and also about acupuncture.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: (In English): In October last year, when Geylang Serai partnered Silver Ribbon to organise the Asia Pacific Mental Wellness Conference with the theme of advocacy, it was attended by many international participants and speakers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: And during that meeting, I launched the Global Mental Health Alliance as well.

sections.label: Self-help groups get $6 million
sections.summary: This Budget allocates $6 million more for self-help groups like MENDAKI, which is good news for the community.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Many methods, programmes and schemes were implemented to help the community improve themselves, their abilities and the status of their families.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: This Budget also allocates $6 million more for self-help groups like MENDAKI and this is also good news for our community.

sections.label: Construction projects brought forward
sections.summary: The Government brought forward building and construction projects planned for 2019 to this year and the following year to help the construction industry.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In fact, the Government has brought forward building and construction projects that were supposed to be done in 2019, to this year and the following year, in order to help our construction industry.

sections.label: ITMs for 23 industry sectors
sections.summary: It contains initiatives to support economic growth by strengthening industry sectors under the ITMs for 23 sectors through tripartite alliance and partnership.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: It is about our future, survival and sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It contains several initiatives to support and assist the growth of our economy by strengthening the industry sectors under the ITMs for 23 industry sectors through the tripartite alliance and partnership.

sections.label: Upskilling, SkillsFuture and budget cuts
sections.summary: Workers can upskill and reskill, the SkillsFuture Leadership Development Initiative will develop 800 Singaporeans, and Ministries face 2% cuts, some in phases.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These workers can plan and start to upskill and reskill to enhance their employability.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I also welcome the SkillsFuture Leadership Development Initiative to develop 800 potential Singaporeans for exposure to international jobs that are well-paying.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As we welcome this, to avoid the situation of talent shortage, the Government could work with companies on job redesigning and rebranding of industries and jobs to attract more locals and Singaporeans working abroad to come back and work at home.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It was also announced that all Ministries would have a 2% cut and that the Health, Home Affairs and Defence Ministries will have a 2% cut in phases.

sections.label: Cost of living mitigating measures
sections.summary: The Government has put in place mitigating measures for low-income families for the diesel cost increase and 30% water conservation tax increase.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I wish to now touch on cost of living.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is notable that for both the diesel cost increase and 30% increase in water conservation tax, the Government has put in place mitigating measures for low-income families.

sections.label: CPF Housing Grant for resale flats
sections.summary: Enhancement of the CPF Housing Grant for resale flats encourages young families to buy resale flats.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Enhancement of the CPF Housing Grant for resale flats encourages young families to buy resale flats.

sections.label: Support for women after childbirth
sections.summary: Such support will enable younger women to stay in the labour market after childbirth and give those who stopped working a reason to return.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Such support will enable younger women to stay in the labour market after childbirth and, for those who had stopped working, a reason to return to work.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is where the employers, those working alongside with them and the entire nation can show better understanding and support to these groups of women who often face challenges raising children.

sections.label: SMEs Go Digital Programme and Technology Hub
sections.summary: The SMEs Go Digital Programme and Technology Hub can help SMEs tap digital solutions, build capabilities and boost productivity, with the Technology Hub connected to SME Centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Some shared with me their challenges how to migrate into the digital space and needing a one-stop solution, among other concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Thus, it is timely that there will be the SMEs Go Digital Programme and Technology Hub which can help SMEs tap on digital solutions, build capabilities and boost productivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Connecting the Technology Hub to the existing network of SME Centres, including USME at NTUC, will also help more businesses to receive advisory, access grant and get step-by-step aid on technology adoption and solutions.

sections.label: Lean Enterprise Development Scheme project
sections.summary: The centres benefit from time and cost savings, nutritious meals and redesigned cooks' jobs, and this Lean Enterprise Development Scheme project shows industry taking the lead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The centres benefit from time and cost savings, properly prepared nutritious meals and, I am quite sure, healthy and less sugar and no fried food, and the jobs of cooks can also be redesigned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This Lean Enterprise Development Scheme project is one good example of how industry can take the lead.

sections.label: Freelancers and self-employed support
sections.summary: There are over 180,000 freelancers and self-employed people, a figure expected to climb, and the speaker will discuss better support for them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I will now move on to speak about how we can better support a new and emerging group of working people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: There are over 180,000 freelancers and the self-employed and, this figure, by many accounts, is expected to climb.

sections.label: Freelancer challenges and responsibilities
sections.summary: Freelancers face strict control by service buyers and must handle their own payment, medical insurance, and CPF savings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Unlike that of a freelancer who can decide to pick up projects or do it anytime, this particular group find that they are strictly controlled by the service buyers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, the onus lies entirely on the workers to ensure that they receive timely payment, manage their own medical and insurance, and contribute to their own CPF savings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Common challenges faced by freelancers include payment, late or sometimes none at all; the need to have intellectual property protection; income instability and running the risk of not saving enough for medical and retirement needs.

sections.label: Self-employed taxi drivers coverage
sections.summary: Self-employed taxi drivers are not covered under any Employment Act, though some can opt for an employee model with HDT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Taxi drivers who are self-employed are not covered under any Employment Act, although recently we have just announced that there is a group of them who can opt to take on the employee model with the new taxi operator HDT.

sections.label: Taxi operators MediSave co-contribution
sections.summary: Taxi operators co-contribute to their hirers' MediSave under the drive-and-save scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Moreover, taxi operators also co-contribute to their hirers' MediSave contribution on this drive-and-save scheme.

sections.label: Manpower Ministry freelancer information gathering
sections.summary: The Manpower Minister said his Ministry is gathering information on the freelancing landscape to understand freelancer profiles and income sources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Recently, the Manpower Minister shared that his Ministry has started to gather information on the changing freelancing landscape in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The purpose is to better understand the profiles of these freelancers, to find out if freelancing is their primary or secondary source of income, as well as the various sectors and occupations they are in.

sections.label: Automation job loss research
sections.summary: One research states that 50% of jobs could be lost to automation within 30 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: According to one research, 50% of the jobs could be lost to automation within 30 years.

sections.label: US freelancer workforce growth
sections.summary: In the US, 33% of workers are freelancers, expected to rise to 40% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Already, in the US, 33% of workers are freelancers, and are expected to rise to 40% in 2020.

sections.label: Freelancer benefits gap
sections.summary: Freelancers lack statutory benefits like annual leave, maternity benefits, ICT reimbursements and paid medical leave, and lack accident, life and outpatient benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Freelancers do not enjoy statutory benefits like the full-time work people do, such as annual leave, maternity benefits, In-camp Training reimbursements or paid medical leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Although MediShield Life provides hospitalisation coverage, freelancers still lack accident, life and especially outpatient benefits that many companies currently provide.

sections.label: Portable benefits and retrenchments
sections.summary: Prof Laura Tyson described a portable, universal, prorated system attached to the worker, and 4,738 workers were retrenched last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Berkeley Prof Laura Tyson has described such a system as portable, attached to the individual worker instead of the employer, universal and prorated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Last year, 4,738 workers were retrenched, 100% more compared to the year 2015.

sections.label: WDA and e2i job help
sections.summary: WDA and e2i told her they organise job fairs but do not offer job search or job matching for individuals like her.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: When she approached WDA and e2i for help, she was told by both organisations that they organise job fairs but do not offer job search or job matching for individuals like her.

sections.label: Bus captain pay rise
sections.summary: As demand for public bus services increases, bus captains' gross monthly pay rose from $2,000 in 2011 to more than $3,000 now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: As the demand for public bus services increases, the gross monthly pay of bus captains has improved dramatically from $2,000 per month in 2011 to more than $3,000 per month now.

sections.label: Sports donations matching fund
sections.summary: An NSA president welcomes $50 million set aside to match sports donations dollar-for-dollar.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: As a president of a National Sports Association (NSA), I welcome the news that $50 million will be set aside to match sports donations dollar-for-dollar.

sections.label: Fund dried up early
sections.summary: Last year the fund dried up as early as September, barely six months from the April start of the financial year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Last year, the fund dried up as early as September, barely six months from the start of the financial year in April.

sections.label: Volleyball courts and sports funding
sections.summary: The speaker asks Sports Singapore to work with schools and the National Parks Board for more volleyball courts, and notes $2.4 billion for CFE strategies over four years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Despite these efforts and our plea to Sports Singapore, many amateur volleyball players cannot find courts to train and to play.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: I hope that Sports Singapore can work with schools to make available more indoor volleyball courts during weekday nights and weekends.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In addition, I hope that Sports Singapore can work with the National Parks Board to designate more segments of the beaches at East Coast, Pasir Ris and so on for beach volleyball.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: These possible collaborations with Sports Singapore and other Government agencies will go a long way towards making Singapore a sporting nation, promoting healthy living, teamwork and better resilience among Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In the Budget, $2.4 billion will be spent over the next four years to implement the CFE strategies, in addition to the S$4.5 billion allocated last year for the ITM programmes.

sections.label: Procurement and outsourced workers' welfare
sections.summary: Procurement is open and transparent for competitive bids, and MOF has engaged the Labour Movement to improve practices and contract clauses for workers' welfare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: They are open and transparent to encourage competitive bids to ensure value for money, but it can be improved upon to ensure outsourced workers' welfare are not compromised by the competitive bids.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I am heartened to share that the Ministry of Finance (MOF) has been very proactive to engage the Labour Movement to improve procurement practices on the ground to promote authentic best sourcing and ensuring fairer contract clauses based on the principle of proportionality to create an environment that will benefit all parties, including workers who can enjoy better terms and conditions.

sections.label: Cleaners' wage model recommendations
sections.summary: Last year, the tripartite committee for cleaners recommended annual increases and bonuses be part of the mandatory wage model.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Last year, the tripartite committee for cleaners recommended annual increases and bonuses to be part of the mandatory wage model.

sections.label: Special Relief Fund review proposal
sections.summary: The Special Relief Fund was set up in 1978 by the Singapore Labour Foundation after the Spyros accident, and the speaker proposes reviewing its criteria for injured workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In 1978, the Special Relief Fund (SRF) was set up by the Singapore Labour Foundation in response to the 1978 Spyros accident.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I would also like to propose that the Government consider reviewing the criteria of the existing SRF to provide immediate relief to affected workers suffering from serious workplace injuries pending the outcome from Workmen's Compensation.

sections.label: Training incentives for low-wage workers
sections.summary: Low-wage workers are most affected by disruptive technologies, and the speaker suggests worker incentives after training, to be studied if the Workfare Income Supplement scheme is reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: There are many more examples about the impact of technologies that will create disruptions to the point that there will be no difference between PMETs and rank-and-file workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: But I reckon that low-wage workers will be affected more and experience a greater impact from these disruptive technologies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: And the best chance for low-wage workers to adapt to these disruptive technologies is by obtaining new skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, some employers are hesitant to send their workers for training, due to concerns that their attrition rate will be high if the worker completes the training and decides to join another company.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: While employers are given incentives to send their workers for training, some incentives should also be given to the workers after they complete their training so that they will remain in their jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This is something that is necessary and should be studied if the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme is being reviewed in the future, so as to encourage workers to stay on with their employers who have sent them for training.

sections.label: Arts, culture and Cultural Matching Fund
sections.summary: The speaker notes arts and culture were mentioned this year, though in one small paragraph, and welcomes a boost for the Cultural Matching Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That time, I had noted that culture was not mentioned much in the speech, but this year, I am thankful and happy that the arts and culture are mentioned, although in only one small paragraph.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But it is good news about a boost for the Cultural Matching Fund.

sections.label: Migrant workers, single parents, displaced workers
sections.summary: It names migrant workers, single parents and workers fearing job loss from technology and artificial intelligence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Migrant workers who have come to Singapore to make a living despite their personal sense of dislocation; single parents and their children who do not enjoy the same benefits of other traditional family units and who struggle to make ends meet; workers who feel that their jobs are at risk because technological advancements and artificial intelligence might make their roles obsolete and losing their sense of place at home, in the society and with themselves.

sections.label: Widening income gap squeeze
sections.summary: It states that with a widening income gap, lower- to middle-income groups feel the squeeze keeping up with change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With the widening income gap, the lower- to middle-income groups constantly feel the squeeze as they try to keep up with change.

sections.label: Privileged speaking up for others
sections.summary: It says the privileged, by wealth, education or race, must speak up for the less earning, less educated and sidelined.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: You can be privileged in terms of wealth or education, or even as a race.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is thus the responsibility of those who are privileged to speak up for those who are not − those who do not earn as much, those who are not as educated, those who are sidelined by our system.

sections.label: Selfishness, violence, pro-business policies
sections.summary: It says this prevents empathy and encourages selfishness, and the Government addresses concerns through pro-business policies and a safety net.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It not only prevents us from being empathetic and compassionate, but encourages selfishness, which can even make violence and brutality justifiable in extreme situations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Government is aware of these concerns and addresses them through pro-business policies and enhancing the safety net.

sections.label: Raising wages, cultural impact study
sections.summary: It asks the Minister how real wages of middle and lower income can be raised and for a study of the cultural impact of economic strategies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As such, I wish to hear more from the Minister on how the real wages of the middle income and lower income can be raised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While CFE focused on economic strategies, it is essential that a study on the cultural impact of these economic strategies be made.

sections.label: Immigration policy cultural impact study
sections.summary: It cites the 1990s to early 2000s expansionary immigration policy, saying an earlier cultural impact study could have mitigated its impact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Another example will be the impact of the expansionary immigration policy of the 1990s to early 2000s, which could be mitigated if we had done a cultural impact study earlier.

sections.label: Education system and creative thinking
sections.summary: The speaker says now is the time to scrutinise the education system and incorporate creative and critical thinking for future generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Such a culture cannot be manifested overnight through new state funding schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There is no better time than now to scrutinise our current education system, incorporate opportunities for creative and critical thinking within it, develop our next generation and generations to come.

sections.label: Arts develop resilience
sections.summary: An arts practitioner attests that the arts develop resilience by opening up critical thinking processes for spectators, audiences, participants and creators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As an arts practitioner, I can attest to the fact that the arts can develop resilience because it opens up our critical thinking processes, be it as a spectator or audience, participant or creator.

sections.label: Bikas Nath poetry prize
sections.summary: Bikas Nath from Bangladesh, a poet and shipyard worker, won first prize at the 2016 Migrant Workers Poetry Competition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Take Bikas Nath from Bangladesh, a poet and shipyard worker who won first prize at the 2016 Migrant Workers Poetry Competition.

sections.label: Active listening and empathy
sections.summary: The speaker says active listening develops empathy and exposes us to views beyond comfort zones, urging the House to keep listening and giving with respect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Active listening allows us to develop empathy and to experience views beyond our comfort zone and echo chambers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I, therefore, urge the House that we continue to listen and give with respect.

sections.label: Safe spaces and inter-community resilience
sections.summary: Building inter-community resilience requires safe spaces with adhered-to rules of engagement, and leadership that inspires citizens to take responsibility for shared growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Similarly, in building inter-community resilience, we need to build such safe spaces where rules of engagement are adhered to, to ensure that our dialogues remain respectful yet robust, critical yet compassionate, passionate yet measured and non-violent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It cannot be stressed enough that leadership plays an important role in motivating and inspiring citizens to take greater responsibility for our shared growth, instead of just focusing on individual success stories.

sections.label: Leaders reduce income gap
sections.summary: In developing long-term strategies to reduce the income gap, leaders can reignite self-belief, meaningfulness and dignity in the people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Rather, in developing long-term strategies to reduce the income gap, our leaders can reignite self-belief, meaningfulness and dignity in the people.

sections.label: CFE change and compassion
sections.summary: The passage urges Singaporeans to be positive forces of change, resilient and compassionate to those who fall through the system's cracks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As our nation moves forward with the proposals by CFE, let us remember to become positive forces of change, to find new ways of seeing and listening, and to always be resilient and compassionate to those who fall through the cracks of the system.

sections.label: Layoffs and PME unemployment
sections.summary: The passage states rising structural forces and unemployment, with a record 19,000 layoffs in 2016 affecting especially PMEs and older workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: From a manpower perspective, there are several challenges for us, I dare say not exhaustive, with the first being rising structural forces and unemployment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: We saw a record 19,000 layoffs in 2016 since the last peak in 2009.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: What has been a worrying trend is that the layoffs affect especially professionals, managers and executives (PMEs) and the slower rate of re-entry into the workforce for this category of workers, especially those who are older.

sections.label: Sector job demand figures
sections.summary: The passage states ICT and healthcare will have 30,000 jobs each, plus needs for precision engineers, rail engineers, data scientists, robot coordinators and early childhood educators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Infocomm technology (ICT) and healthcare sectors have highlighted there will be 30,000 jobs each.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: We also need 3,000 precision engineers, 1,000 rail engineers and 22,000 data scientists and robot coordinators in the manufacturing sector by 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: There is also a need for 4,000 early childhood educators.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit top-ups proposal
sections.summary: The passage suggests Government SkillsFuture Credit top-ups of $500 every three to five years to encourage personal responsibility in continuing education and lifelong learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: To address this, I suggest for the Government to provide SkillsFuture Credit top-ups of $500 in intervals every three to five years so as to encourage Singaporeans to take personal responsibility in their continuing education and training, embrace a spirit of lifelong learning and stay ready, relevant and resilient.

sections.label: Attention to laid-off PMETs
sections.summary: The passage submits that with about 70% of those laid off last year being PMETs, particular attention is needed for long-term unemployed and mature PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: With about 70% of those laid off last year being PMETs, I submit that we need to pay particular attention to this group and, especially those who are long-term unemployed and mature PMEs.

sections.label: Helping PMEs into second careers
sections.summary: The passage hopes the Government helps PMEs transit into second careers by exploring job and skill adjacency so they can move into new roles using their experience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: There is strong inertia from many PMEs to explore new industries due to the high opportunity cost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: It is with this in mind that I hope the Government can look into helping PMEs transit into second careers more seamlessly by exploring the adjacency of jobs and the adjacency of skills so that these PMEs can move into, move across or move up into new roles which capitalise on their acquired skills and knowledge so that they can even enter mid-career and be given credits for their experience.

sections.label: Tripartite partners and future jobs
sections.summary: Tripartite partners must work with higher learning institutions, industry partners, stakeholders and research firms to place the future unemployed into future jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: By doing this, we can better help our workers prepare for these future jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Hence, the tripartite partners must work closely together with higher learning institutions, industry partners and stakeholders, as well as research and consultancy firms to collect needed information and not just place the current unemployed into current jobs, but the future unemployed into future jobs.

sections.label: SkillsFuture top-up and PME help
sections.summary: The speaker suggests topping up $500 into SkillsFuture credit every three to five years and exploring help for PMEs into adjacent jobs and skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Fourth, I also suggest that the Government top up $500 into the SkillsFuture credit every three to five years to encourage Singaporeans to take personal responsibility for their own career development, embrace the spirit of lifelong learning and stay relevant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Fifth, while we introduce and execute the various programmes, we must consider how to look after all segments of the workforce, including low-income workers and PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I hope the Government can explore how to help PMEs into adjacent jobs and adjacent skills, so that they can transit into a second career seamlessly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: (In English): Mdm Speaker, the challenge for Singapore in 2017 and beyond is how we are able to navigate the occasional gusty winds and flooding downpours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Although we have weathered a variety of economic calamities in the past decade alone, it does not mean we will automatically survive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The challenge that confronts us this decade will be somewhat different and diverse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The "killer app" is how we can, as one country and one people, stay not just ready, relevant and resilient but have the necessary ability, agility and adaptability to navigate and ride on the ebb and flow.

sections.label: Budget and Net Investment Income
sections.summary: This year's Budget is about $70 billion, of which $14 billion comes from Net Investment Income, one dollar in five.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: But let us take a look at our Budget position carefully.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: This year, we have a Budget of about $70 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Out of that $70 billion, $14 billion comes from our Net Investment Income (NII), which means that for every five dollars we spend, one dollar comes from the savings, or the income from our savings, to be more precise.

sections.label: Top four revenue streams
sections.summary: The top four revenue streams are NII, corporate tax, GST and income tax, with NII the number one income stream this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The top four revenue streams of our Budget are NII, corporate tax, GST and income tax.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: This year, the number one income stream, out of these four, is NII.

sections.label: Budget after Net Investment Income
sections.summary: Even after accounting for NII, less than $2 billion is budgeted for.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Even after accounting for NII, we have less than $2 billion budgeted for.

sections.label: Workfare Income Supplement cost
sections.summary: The Workfare Income Supplement programme costs $600 million to $700 million.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: One programme, like Workfare Income Supplement, costs us $600 million to $700 million.

sections.label: U-Save rebates for lower income
sections.summary: The passage asks why money is spent on increased U-Save rebates to protect lower income from average price increases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: If this is so, why do we spend all the money that we spend for that increase in the U-Save rebates to make sure that even though prices may increase on average, we will take care of the lower income first?

sections.label: Government targeting help for people
sections.summary: The passage states the Government is not cynical and its targeted help is because it feels the people's pain.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: No, this is not a cynical Government and it will be wrong for us to impute our own perverse motive on the Government.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: It is targeted to help precisely because we feel the pain for our people.

sections.label: Long tail spending commitments
sections.summary: The passage states spending commitments have long tails, reducing future white space and flexibility for contingencies and opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Every time we make a commitment to spend on a policy, it has a long tail, which means that there are future commitments that we need to adhere to, to keep our words to our people.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Every time we have a long tail, it eats into what, in budgetary terms, we call the "white space" for the future, which means that the more we commit upfront with a long tail, the less degree of flexibility we have going forward to meet contingencies and to seize opportunities.

sections.label: NTUC priorities jobs
sections.summary: The passage states NTUC has three priorities for the year: jobs, jobs and jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In NTUC, we have three priorities for this year − jobs, jobs and jobs.

sections.label: Digital and ITMs implementation
sections.summary: The passage asks how digital can transcend geography and create advantages, tied to implementing ITMs covering 80% of sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: How do we use digital to again transcend our geography, create new resources and create new competitive advantages for ourselves?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But the thing that ties these all together is simply this − our ability to implement our ITMs well, because they cover 80% of our sectors.

sections.label: NTUC raising funds for training
sections.summary: The passage states NTUC is raising $200 million to work with IHLs on modules to help tomorrow's unemployed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Most importantly, we have to prepare to help tomorrow's unemployed into tomorrow's job, and that we have to do well to overcome the potential structural unemployment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This is the reason why NTUC is raising $200 million, on top of what we have in our NTUC Education and Training Fund, to work with our IHLs on national modules, stackable modules, and just-in-time modules.

sections.label: MOM workgroup on structural changes
sections.summary: MOM is initiating a workgroup with businesses and the Labour Movement to study long-term structural changes to the employment market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We need new mental models to help these workers protect their legal rights, financial rights, help them to plan for their retirement and so forth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This is why MOM is initiating a workgroup with the businesses, with the Labour Movement to study the implications of such long-term structural changes to our employment market, and we have to get this right.

sections.label: Businesses re-examining processes, 23 ITMs
sections.summary: Each business must re-examine its processes with workers and management to raise productivity, with 23 ITMs moving the needle for 80% of the market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Macro-policy measures enable, but what is most important is that each and every business has to re-examine its business processes together with the workers, and together with management to raise the productivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This is where the 23 ITMs come in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: If we get this right, we move the needle for 80% of the market.

sections.label: Dollar more means dollar less
sections.summary: Going forward, every dollar given more to someone means a dollar less to someone else.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Going forward, for every dollar that we give more to someone, it actually means a dollar less to someone else.

sections.label: Leaning forward to weaker segment
sections.summary: The government will lean forward for the weaker and poorer segment, meaning the more privileged will foot a bigger bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: That we will lean forward for the weaker segment of our population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And because we say we lean forward to the weaker segment of our population, the poorer segment of our population, it means that some of us who are more privileged will have to foot a bigger bill.

sections.label: Concentrating help on those most needy
sections.summary: Whatever is collected is concentrated and focused on helping those who need it most.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Whatever we collect, we concentrate and focus the help on those who need it most.

sections.label: Angst over water price increase
sections.summary: The speaker feels compelled to talk about this after hearing much, understanding people's angst over the water price increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: I feel compelled to talk about this because I have heard much over the last two days and the last one week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: I can understand the angst of our people with the water price increase.

sections.label: Water existential to country's survival
sections.summary: The passage asks Members of the House whether they agree that water is existential to the country's survival.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: As Members of this House, do we agree that water is existential to our country's survival?

sections.label: Seventeen reservoirs today
sections.summary: The passage states that there are 17 reservoirs today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The answer is we have 17 reservoirs today.

sections.label: Two-thirds land area catchment
sections.summary: The passage states that two-thirds of Singapore's entire land area today are water catchment areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Two-thirds of the entire land area in Singapore today are water catchment areas.

sections.label: NEWater plants before 2000
sections.summary: The passage states that NEWater plants did not exist before 2000, as Members heard from Minister Masagos.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: NEWater plants, as Members have heard from Minister Masagos, did not exist before 2000.

sections.label: Catchment area and Linggui Reservoir
sections.summary: The passage states the water catchment area cannot be increased by much, and Linggui Reservoir's catchment area is twice the size of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We cannot possibly increase the water catchment area in Singapore by much.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And just as a point of illustration, Linggui Reservoir, the catchment area of Linggui Reservoir, is twice the size of Singapore − twice.

sections.label: Leaky pipes and NEWater plant
sections.summary: The passage states that losing 5% of water through leaky pipes requires building one more NEWater plant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: If we lose 5% of our water through leaky pipes, we need to build one more NEWater plant.

sections.label: Thirty percent over 17 years
sections.summary: Thirty percent over 17 years works out to about 1.6% a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Thirty percent over 17 years is about 1.6% a year.

sections.label: First Water Agreement concluded
sections.summary: The first Water Agreement with Malaysia was concluded on 31 August 2011 without making headlines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The most significant thing that happened in 2011, without it making to the headlines of The Straits Times, was the fact that on 31 August 2011, we concluded the first Water Agreement with Malaysia without it making to the headlines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Last year, I visited the Public Utilities Board (PUB) union and I spoke to the management and the workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: I similarly challenged them, that in 45 years' time, 2061, I hope that it will also be a non-event when our second Water Agreement with Malaysia expires.

sections.label: Responsible government prices essentials
sections.summary: A responsible government prices essentials properly rather than distorting the market and adding subsidies that burden future generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: A responsible government is one that prices the essentials properly, and not distort the market, leading to more subsidies that will burden our future generations.

sections.label: Not a wait-and-see Budget
sections.summary: A wait-and-see Budget would not require carbon pricing mechanisms, diesel tax or water tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: If this is a wait-and-see Budget, we would not have to put in place the mechanisms for carbon pricing, we would not have to talk about diesel tax, we would not have to talk about water tax.

sections.label: Permanent 2% budget cap cut
sections.summary: Minister Heng introduced a permanent 2% cut on budget caps for all Ministries and agencies.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Minister Heng boldly introduced a permanent 2% cut on the budget caps for all Ministries and agencies.

sections.label: 700 million for construction industry
sections.summary: The Government will bring forward $700 million in infrastructure projects, though this is not enough to impact the construction industry.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For the construction industry, I am pleased that the Government will bring forward $700 million in infrastructure projects, including construction of community centres and facilities for sports and the arts.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: At the back of my mind, I was thinking, hopefully, this would include a new swimming complex in Yishun which I have been asking for.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But ultimately, for the construction industry, $700 million is not really enough to make an impact.

sections.label: Foreign worker levy and diesel tax
sections.summary: A request that the Government defer the 2017 foreign workers' levy increase for affected firms, as was done for marine and process sectors.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2017, their foreign workers' levy will go up again and they will be affected by the diesel tax, too.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Government consider deferring their levy increase till better times, like for the marine and process sectors?

sections.label: SSI biomechanic duties
sections.summary: The SSI biomechanic assigned to SSA also has other NSA responsibilities, not only SSA needs.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For example, the Singapore Sports Institute's (SSI's) biomechanic who is assigned to SSA does not look after just the needs of SSA but also has other NSA responsibilities.

sections.label: US electric vehicle tax credits
sections.summary: In the US, the federal government provides tax credits of up to US$7,500 per electric vehicle purchased.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For example, in the US, the federal government provides tax credits of up to US$7,500 for each electric vehicle purchased.

sections.label: Water price increase production costs
sections.summary: The water price increase will raise production costs, with a 2% to 4% increase in semi-conductor production.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Five, the water price increase will have an impact on production costs, that is, 2% to 4% increase in production of semi-conductors, for example, I was told.

sections.label: Water recycling in semi-conductor sector
sections.summary: Many companies already recycle water, about 40% in the semi-conductor sector, and the Government is asked to help do more.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Many of our companies are already doing water recycling and I hope the Government can work with the industry to see how we can do more water recycling to retain our competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I was told that, currently, about 40% of the water is recycled in the semi-conductor sector.

sections.label: Construction industry government projects funding
sections.summary: The $700 million in brought-forward Government projects is not enough to be shared among the many construction companies.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For the construction industry, although the Government has brought forward Government projects worth $700 million, with so many companies in the construction industry, the $700 million is not enough to be shared by them.

sections.label: Budget surplus and assistance
sections.summary: The speaker hopes savings improve cross-agency collaboration and creative thinking, noting a $5.2 billion surplus larger than the estimated $3.5 billion for FY2016.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope that the Government can make use of the money saved to improve cross-agency collaboration and cultivate creative thinking amongst civil servants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It is reassuring to know that we are recording a Budget surplus of $5.2 billion, larger than the estimated surplus of $3.5 billion for financial year 2016, so that the Government will have the ability and, I am sure, the willingness, too, to step in with more assistance should the conditions turn further south in this volatile and uncertain environment.

sections.label: Budget caps cut, fewer tenders
sections.summary: A proposed 2% downward adjustment to budget caps of all Ministries and Organs of State may decrease Government projects available for public tender.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With the proposed 2% downward adjustment to the budget caps of all Ministries and Organs of State, we can foresee a decrease in Government projects available for public tender.

sections.label: Timing of increase
sections.summary: The timing of the increase is of concern.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The timing of the increase is of concern.

sections.label: Infrastructure projects and Buy Singapore
sections.summary: Bringing forward $700 million of infrastructure projects will help construction, and a "Buy Singapore" requirement for goods and services could boost local demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Bringing forward $700 million worth of infrastructure projects will certainly help the construction sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Government can do more to boost local demand by including a "Buy Singapore" requirement. "Buy Singapore" should apply to both goods and services.

sections.label: Proudly Singapore labels and sustainability
sections.summary: The Government can award qualifying companies "Proudly Made in Singapore" or "Proudly Singapore" marks, and "Buy Singapore" ties in with environmental sustainability measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In addition, the Government can award companies which meet prerequisite standards within their industries with an official "Proudly Made in Singapore" product stamp or "Proudly Singapore" service logo.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Hopefully, in time, the "Made in Singapore" label will be as trusted and respected as "Made in Japan" or "Made in Germany" labels. "Buy Singapore" also ties in with another important national objective − environmental sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Minister Heng has highlighted the importance of sustainability in his speech and introduced measures targeted towards more sustainable business practices and consumer behaviour with the increase in water pricing, introduction of carbon tax and promoting the use of cleaner vehicles.

sections.label: Buying local reduces carbon footprint
sections.summary: Buying products made or manufactured closer to home would be one way of reducing one's carbon footprint.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Buying products that are made or manufactured closer to home would be one way of reducing one's carbon footprint.

sections.label: Adults setting environmental examples
sections.summary: Adults must set good examples and lead in protecting the environment, and the Government is urged to support community-based environmental projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We, as adults, must set good examples and take the lead in our family lives and in our professions to protect our environment for our present and future generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to continue to provide more support to community-based projects that are environmentally beneficial.

sections.label: Budget needs mindset change
sections.summary: The Budget would not achieve its objectives if implemented and relied on without a mindset change.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We cannot think like we used to think.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I submit that the Budget would not achieve its objectives if we implemented and relied on the Budget measures without a mindset change.

sections.label: Mindset change as game changer
sections.summary: Without a mindset change the Budget is just schemes and measures, but with one it can be a powerful game changer for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A mindset change is what we need, because if we do not change our mindsets, the Budget will just be a bag of schemes and measures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But if we change our mindsets, it can be turned into a powerful game changer for Singapore.

sections.label: Public Service implementation of schemes
sections.summary: The speaker fears the seriousness of the message may not have filtered through to every level of the Public Service implementing the schemes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Whilst we hear in this House Ministerial speeches and Members' speeches about what we believe in, about the seriousness of the global situation and our dependence on other external factors, I fear that the seriousness of the message may not have filtered through to every level of the Public Service.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If they believe in the schemes achieving what the schemes are meant to achieve, then the way they implement the schemes will be very different.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It will not be just a question, I hope, of checking checklists, ticking the boxes or keeping an eye on key performance indicators (KPIs).

sections.label: Employers committing to Singaporean Core
sections.summary: The speaker hopes all businesses, local or MNCs, will commit to developing the Singaporean Core, welcoming partners but not raiders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And how can employers be committed if they are not so persuaded by the persons who grant them the grants and make the schemes and measures available to them?

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope that all businesses, local or MNCs, will commit to developing the Singaporean Core.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I want to say we welcome partners, but not raiders.

sections.label: Accommodation of disability and PSD recruitment
sections.summary: The speaker asks only for accommodation of their disability and was encouraged by PSD's 2016 plans to recruit persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We ask only for accommodation of our disability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We were, therefore, encouraged when the Public Service Division (PSD) announced in 2016 its plans to recruit persons with disabilities.

sections.label: PSD and agency human resource values
sections.summary: The speaker observes that progress requires human resource teams of PSD and agencies to share the Head of Civil Service's values and commitment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, my observations are that unless the human resource teams of PSD and the respective agencies share the same values and commitment as the Head of the Civil Service, we will not be able to progress.

sections.label: Government example on employing disabled
sections.summary: When the Government sets the example, it stands on stronger moral grounds to urge the private sector to employ able persons with disabled bodies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When the Government sets the example, it stands on stronger moral grounds to urge the private sector to employ able persons with disabled bodies.

sections.label: A caring three-care Budget
sections.summary: The speaker categorises this Budget as a caring Budget that cares for the future, the people and the environment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In fact, this is one Budget that I categorise as a caring Budget − a three "care" Budget - it cares for the future, it cares for the people and it cares for the environment.

sections.label: Inflationary impact of water and diesel tax
sections.summary: The passage states the first point is the inflationary impact of the water as well as the diesel tax.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: First is the inflationary impact of the water as well as the diesel tax.

sections.label: Cost of living and water price urgency
sections.summary: The speaker dreads the cost-of-living impact, cites electricity tariff rises, and questions the urgency of raising water price after 17 years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I dread to think about how this will impact the cost of living.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This year, we started off by having to cope with the rise in electricity tariffs by an average of 5.7% or 1.07 cents per kilowatt hour for the period of January-March, compared to the previous quarter, as announced by power provider SP Services on 30 December 2016.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The big question is, so, why does there seem to be such an urgency to raise the water price after 17 years?

sections.label: Rebates versus long-term increase effects
sections.summary: Residents complain rebates are one-off while increase effects are long term, but many ignored the permanent GST Voucher and U-Save increase.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The commonly heard complaint from residents is that the rebates are sort of one-off on a year-to-year basis, but the effects of the increase are long term and would stay long after the rebates have expired.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But many had ignored the fact that the Minister had also announced a permanent increase in Goods and Services Tax (GST) Voucher and U-Save on top of the one-off GST Voucher special payment.

sections.label: Stanford study on tiered water pricing
sections.summary: A Stanford University Water in the West Programme study finds tiered water pricing is a critical tool for incentivising water conservation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: According to a research study by Stanford University's Water in the West Programme, tiered water pricing is a critical tool in incentivising water conservation.

sections.label: China local government water pricing
sections.summary: Local governments experimented with multiple-tiered water pricing for households and industry, and from 2015 all localities adopted the new system for China.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The local governments experimented with multiple-tiered pricing systems for urban households and industrial users, charging higher prices for higher water consumption.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And these reforms have found to achieve their desired outcomes and, as such, from 2015, all localities started to adopt the new water pricing system for China.

sections.label: Inflationary impact and diesel vehicles
sections.summary: This is another inflationary impact on people and businesses, with about 185,000 Singapore-registered diesel vehicles on the roads.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This is another inflationary impact on the people and on businesses as a whole.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There are about 185,000 Singapore-registered diesel vehicles on the roads.

sections.label: Knock-on effect and road tax rebates
sections.summary: The knock-on effect would be across the board, and the Budget gives commercial diesel vehicles a 100% road tax rebate for one year and partial rebates for two more.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The knock-on effect would thus be across the board.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I know the Budget is giving help to businesses to adjust by providing commercial diesel vehicles with a 100% road tax rebate for one year, and a partial road tax rebate for another two years.

sections.label: Question on predicted inflationary effect
sections.summary: The Member asks the Finance Minister the predicted inflationary effect of the water price increase and diesel duty on the Singapore economy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Taken together, may I ask the Finance Minister what is the predicted inflationary effect of both the water price increase as well as the diesel duty implementation on the Singapore economy in the near and medium term?

sections.label: Solar energy and carbon tax revenue
sections.summary: The Member feels more resources should explore solar energy, and hopes carbon tax revenue helps businesses innovate with cleaner, greener energy sources.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I feel that we should spend more resources to explore the use of solar energy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There is a lot of scope and potential for us now to tap on solar energy as the cost of solar panels has dropped over the years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Another positive outcome of implementing the carbon tax would be that it serves as a motivation for companies and businesses to innovate with cleaner, greener energy sources.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I hope the Government can use the revenue collected under this carbon tax to help businesses with this endeavour and also promote green innovation.

sections.label: Global Innovation Alliance Budget measures
sections.summary: The Budget presents measures under the Global Innovation Alliance to help businesses and employees operate overseas.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In a globalised society, it is important to be exposed to foreign countries, whether it is culture, education system, the job market and so forth.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I note that the Budget presents a slew of measures under the Global Innovation Alliance to help businesses and employees to operate overseas.

sections.label: INSEAD Global Innovation Index 2016 rankings
sections.summary: The INSEAD Global Innovation Index 2016 ranked Switzerland first, Sweden second, the UK third, the US fourth, Finland fifth and Singapore sixth.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In the INSEAD Global Innovation Index 2016, Switzerland was ranked first, Sweden was ranked second, the UK third, with the US fourth, Finland fifth and Singapore sixth.

sections.label: SMEs Go Digital Programme
sections.summary: The proposed SMEs Go Digital Programme will help SMEs enhance digital capabilities, improve business operations and provide better customer services.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The proposed SMEs Go Digital Programme will definitely help our SMEs to enhance their digital capabilities and improve business operations, providing better customer services in turn.

sections.label: Construction ITM and Productivity Fund
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government can co-chair with CIJC to develop the construction ITM, and notes the Budget's $150-million Public Sector Productivity Fund.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
