sentences.text: With that said, I also hope that the Government can co-chair with CIJC to jointly develop the construction ITM.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: I am pleased to note that the Budget has provided a $150-million Public Sector Productivity Fund to allow Government agencies to procure innovative and productive construction solutions.

sections.label: Bukit Panjang CC Green Mark award
sections.summary: Bukit Panjang CC was the first CC to attain the BCA Green Mark Gold Plus award after installing solar panels and retrofitting, incurring about $400,000.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Bukit Panjang CC was the first CC in Singapore to attain the Building and Construction Authority's Green Mark Gold Plus award under the Non-residential Existing Building Category after its installation of solar panels and retrofitting of its existing building.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The Bukit Panjang CC incurred an expenditure of about $400,000 to install energy-efficient air-conditioning systems, light emitting diode (LED) lightings, water saving sanitary appliances, as well as a green wall to reduce heat transfer.

sections.label: LED light installations in HDB blocks
sections.summary: 1.18 million LED lights have been installed in HDB common corridors, staircase landings and void decks, with another 730,000 being installed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: To date, we have installed 1.18 million LED lights at the common corridors, staircase landings and void decks of HDB blocks, and are presently installing another 730,000 LED lights to replace lightings at the outdoor open areas.

sections.label: Additional ARF on motorcycles
sections.summary: Motorcycles with OMV above $10,000 pay additional ARF of 100% per dollar above $10,000, on top of $3,250 on the first $10,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Motorcycles with an Open Market Value (OMV) in excess of $10,000 are liable to pay additional ARF on a 100% basis for every dollar above $10,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: This is in addition to the $3,250 that is now payable on the first $10,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: This represents a significant increase in price for higher end motorcycles.

sections.label: COE price rise
sections.summary: COE prices rose from $889 in January 2010 to $6,412 in February 2017, more than six times in seven years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: COE prices have risen from $889 in January 2010 to $6,412 in February 2017, a multiple of more than six times in seven years.

sections.label: Special Tax reduction for taxis
sections.summary: The Government offset this with a permanent reduction of the Special Tax for taxis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The Government has offset this with a permanent reduction of the Special Tax for taxis.

sections.label: Budget measures and family distress
sections.summary: Near-term Budget measures and existing schemes help relieve living cost pressures, but the speaker hopes the Government will do more to identify distressed families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The near-term measures announced in this Budget, together with existing schemes, are helpful in relieving some of the living cost pressures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: But I hope the Government will do more by proactively identifying families showing signs of distress, such as escalating arrears in rent, utilities and service and conservancy charges.

sections.label: Elderly healthcare out-of-pocket expenditure
sections.summary: An elderly person's average out-of-pocket healthcare expenditure is 7.9%, higher than a younger person's 4.4% to 5.5%, after subsidies and MediSave deductions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Already, on average, an elderly's out-of-pocket expenditure in healthcare is 7.9%, much higher than a younger person's which ranges between 4.4% and 5.5%, after taking into account Government subsidies and MediSave deductions.

sections.label: Healthcare spending and old-age support
sections.summary: Government healthcare spending per capita rose from an average of $488 in 2003 to $1,962 in 2016, while the old-age support ratio is falling.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The Government's healthcare spending per capita has also been rising from an average of $488 in 2003 to $1,962 in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The old-age support ratio, however, is steadily falling from 9:1 in 2000 to an expected 2:1 in 2030.

sections.label: Healthcare worker and aged care needs
sections.summary: MOH estimated about 30,000 more healthcare workers by 2020, one-third for aged care, with about 75% of the 2015 workforce Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Health has estimated that it would need an addition of about 30,000 more healthcare workers by 2020 and, of this 30,000, about one-third is estimated to be dedicated towards the aged care sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Currently, in 2015, about 75% of the healthcare workforce are Singaporeans.

sections.label: Shifting eldercare away from institutions
sections.summary: Land scarcity and manpower shortage require shifting the eldercare model away from institutions, reserving residential institutions for elderly needing highly intensive care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: With land scarcity and manpower shortage, the eldercare model needs to shift away from institutions and reserve the residential institutions for the elderly who need highly intensive care.

sections.label: Government leading smart homes for seniors
sections.summary: It asks whether the Government could take a point position and lead nationwide implementation of smart homes for seniors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Could the Government take a point position and lead a nationwide implementation of smart homes for seniors?

sections.label: Redirecting investment to age in place
sections.summary: It asks whether the Government could redirect investment from building new institutions to enable more elderly to live independently at home and age in place.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Therefore, could the Government look into enabling this?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: So, instead of investing money on building new institutions, could we redirect some of this investment to enable more elderly to live independently in their own homes, so that they can continue to go about their daily lives, continue to be part of the neighbourhood that they are so familiar with and truly age in place?

sections.label: Rallying volunteers for unfulfilled needs
sections.summary: It asks how to rally people together to address unfulfilled needs, giving examples of young retirees, housewives and students volunteering.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: How can we rally them together and better organise ourselves to address unfulfilled needs?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: For example, can young retirees who drive help to ferry the older and frailer seniors to their medical appointments?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Can housewives with spare capacity help to fetch children, whose families are for some reason unavailable, to and from school?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Can well-performing students help to run enrichment and reading programmes for children of low-income or dysfunctional families on a weekly basis?

sections.label: Identifying needs and recognising volunteers
sections.summary: It suggests identifying unfulfilled needs, articulating volunteer roles, and better recognising individual efforts so Singaporeans find no reason to say no.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Perhaps, on top of the grants to charities and schemes to encourage donations, we need to identify areas of unfulfilled needs, clearly articulate the roles that volunteers can assume, and devise a better way of recognising individual efforts in the community so that Singaporeans will find no reason to say no.

sections.label: Rising spending, falling working population
sections.summary: Spending is expected to rise, especially on health and social areas, while the working population is likely to fall, and taxes cannot be raised too much.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Our spending on a wide range of areas is expected to rise, including, in particular, on health and social spending, as our population ages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: At the same time, our working population is likely to fall, creating a double whammy as our income tax base grows narrower and our spending needs rise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There are also limits to how much we can raise taxes, as we need to remain attractive as a business destination for the best companies and global corporations can simply choose to do business elsewhere if Singapore becomes unattractive, relative to other destinations.

sections.label: Special Employment Credit scheme
sections.summary: The speaker supports in principle the Special Employment Credit scheme, which encourages the employment of older workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In this context, one of the schemes that I support in principle is the Special Employment Credit scheme which encourages the employment of older workers.

sections.label: Rise in water prices
sections.summary: The 30% water price rise drew attention, with average bills lower by about $1 for 1-room and 2-room flats and higher for larger flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: One matter that has received a lot of attention is the rise in water prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This has been extensively discussed in many forums as the headline rise of 30% was seen as high by many Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For example, I think people mostly understand now that for most people living in 1-room and 2-room flats, the average water bill will actually be lower by around $1 a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For those living in 3-room flats, it may rise by around $2 a month; for those living in 4-room flats, around $5 and, for those living in 5-room flats, around $8.

sections.label: Doubling of infant care places
sections.summary: The Budget doubles infant care places over the next four years, a measure the speaker welcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And if you go before childcare, there is infant care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, in this Budget, we have a doubling of places for infant care over the next four years, which is a measure I welcome.

sections.label: Infant care places by 2020
sections.summary: The speaker is grateful for the initiative to increase infant care places to over 8,000 by 2020, important for working mothers and single-parent families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In this year's Budget, I am grateful for the Government's initiative to increase infant care places to over 8,000 by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This will be particularly important for working mothers and single-parent families.

sections.label: Grants for post-secondary education
sections.summary: More grants are available for post-secondary education, especially at ITE, polytechnic or university, and the speaker encourages youths to take these opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: At the other side of the educational range, there are also more grants for post-secondary education, particularly for those going to the Institute of Technical Education, polytechnic or university.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I strongly encourage all our youths to strive for post-secondary education and to take advantage of the opportunities made available.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In an ever-changing world, education and relevant skills-based training will be important for us and our children to keep up with the new opportunities available.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Government will provide assistance and opportunities and we should, at the same time, not be afraid to learn and do so continuously.

sections.label: Mother's brain tumour hospital bill
sections.summary: Mr Tok's mother had two brain tumour surgeries at Tan Tock Seng Hospital, 58 days in a B2 ward, about $102,000 bill, and zero cash outlay.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Last year, Mr Tok's mother was hospitalised for two separate brain tumour surgeries at Tan Tock Seng Hospital.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: She was hospitalised for 58 days and her medical bill was about $102,000.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: She stayed in a B2 ward and, after Government subsidies, MediShield Life and MediSave deductions, his family's cash outlay was zero.

sections.label: Global and Singapore medical inflation
sections.summary: A study found global medical inflation in 2015 was 10% while in Singapore it was 15%.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: According to a study, global medical inflation in 2015 was 10% but, in Singapore, it was 15%.

sections.label: Private hospital surgery bill size
sections.summary: The Ministry of Health website shows the 75th percentile bill size in private hospital for this surgery is between $4,000 and $9,000.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Health (MOH) website shows that the 75th percentile bill size in private hospital for this surgery is between $4,000 and $9,000.

sections.label: Over-consumption and insurance premiums
sections.summary: Over-consumption and increased medical cost will definitely lead to an increase in insurance premiums.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Over-consumption and increased medical cost will definitely lead to an increase in insurance premiums.

sections.label: Family doctors and affordable healthcare
sections.summary: Family doctors can play a greater role in long-term patient care, and the speaker hopes efforts ensure healthcare stays affordable as people age rapidly.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Our family doctors can play a greater role in the long-term care of the patient.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, I hope we spare no efforts in ensuring that our healthcare system remains truly affordable for Singaporeans, especially when our people are ageing rapidly.

sections.label: Efficiency compromising compassion
sections.summary: The speaker is concerned that in pursuing efficiency, a key value of compassion has been compromised, creating a system without a heart.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My concern is that in the pursuit of efficiency, we have compromised a key value − compassion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In our pursuit to automate most things, we now have a system without a heart.

sections.label: Computer-generated letter unknown
sections.summary: The answer was that they did not know the letter was sent because it was computer-generated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The answer was that they did not know the letter was sent as it was computer-generated.

sections.label: Monkey culling concerns
sections.summary: Professors and NGOs voiced concerns and concluded, based on science, that culling monkeys makes the situation worse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Professors at our local universities and non-government organisations (NGOs) have all voiced our concerns and, based on science, have concluded that the culling of monkeys actually makes the situation worse.

sections.label: Cross-island line engagement
sections.summary: The cross-island line saga shows the need to engage the community and get feedback before deciding, not after.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The cross-island line saga is perhaps the best example of how we should have engaged the wider community and how we should have done sessions to get feedback to make a decision, rather than make a decision and then call for a dialogue.

sections.label: Feedback before First Reading
sections.summary: The speaker suggests all Bills be put on REACH for extensive public consultation before the First Reading.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We need to develop a culture where they are not penalised for being different and where they are giving some flexibility when processing cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I suggest that all Bills that we debate in this House are put on the feedback unit Reaching Everyone for Active Citizenry @ Home (REACH) for extensive public consultation before the First Reading.

sections.label: Early childhood consultation report
sections.summary: The Early Childhood Development Agency report of 20 November 2015 covered the Public Consultation on the Proposed Early Childhood Development Centres Regulatory Framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: An excellent example is the report done by the Early Childhood Development Agency published on 20 November 2015 with regard to the Public Consultation on Proposed Early Childhood Development Centres Regulatory Framework, the Bill that we debated just a few days ago.

sections.label: Draft Budget Statement release
sections.summary: The speaker repeats a suggestion that a draft Budget Statement be released so the public can make suggestions before the Budget is finalised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I suggested this last year and I will suggest it again.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We should release a draft Budget Statement so the public has a chance to make suggestions before we finalise the Budget.

sections.label: Public servants and ground policies
sections.summary: The speaker urges public servants to see how policies affect people on the ground and suggests setting up more committees like two named panels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I urge public servants to also embark on this journey and see how their policies affect the people on the ground.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I suggest we set up more committees like the Animal Welfare Legislation Review Committee and the Active Mobility Advisory Panel.

sections.label: Public servants and civil society activists
sections.summary: The speaker's last suggestion is for public servants to work more closely with civil society activists.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My last suggestion is for public servants to work more closely with civil society activists.

sections.label: Singapore trust rankings and institutions
sections.summary: Singapore is the fifth most high-trust nation, with 30% of respondents believing the system was failing and 43% uncertain.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Apparently, Singapore is the fifth most high-trust nation, outranked only by India, China, Indonesia and the United Arab Emirates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Compared to the global average of more than 50%, only 30% of respondents in Singapore believed the system was failing while 43% said they were uncertain.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To be a country where public trust in all four institutions is still above 50% is now a thing of great value in an uncertain world.

sections.label: Global trust gap widening
sections.summary: The global trust gap between the informed public and the mass population has widened significantly, with the biggest disparities in the US, UK and France.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The global gap between the level of trust felt by the informed public and that felt by the mass population has widened significantly, with the biggest disparities in the US, UK and France.

sections.label: Singapore mass population trust shift
sections.summary: Singapore's mass population respondents still placed it in the top five, but in 2017 they slid from Trusters to Neutrals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In Singapore, the difference is still not so stark.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our mass population respondents still trusted Singapore enough to place it in the top five.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But 2017 was also the first time when our mass population respondents slid from being in the category of Trusters to the category of Neutrals.

sections.label: Pace of change in business
sections.summary: Overwhelmingly, 70% of them believed the pace of change in business and industry was too fast.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Overwhelmingly, 70% of them believed the pace of change in business and industry was too fast.

sections.label: Bottom 10% sandwich class
sections.summary: The bottom 10% sandwich class hold full-time jobs and try to support their families but remain stuck in the poverty cycle.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The bottom 10% sandwich class who hold full-time jobs, who are making a real effort to support their family but still cannot seem to break their poverty cycle.

sections.label: Larger paradigm-shifting systems changes
sections.summary: The speaker argues that to avoid toxic distrust, Singapore must take larger paradigm-shifting systems-level changes sooner rather than later to help the least.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There are far more convincing experts in this House and beyond who can make that case.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But I will, nevertheless, go on a limb to state my assessment that if we do not want our system to slide into the levels of toxic distrust we see elsewhere, we must move away from safe, small, incremental steps and take larger paradigm-shifting changes on a systems level to help the least in our land.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And we should take those steps sooner rather than later.

sections.label: Salary cap disqualifies applicant
sections.summary: A frontline officer tells her that her $1,600 monthly salary disqualifies her under the $1,500 income cap and advises her to stop work, apply for a rental flat and restart work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The frontline officer tells her that $1,600 monthly salary disqualifies her under the $1,500 income cap.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: She is advised to beat the system by stopping work, applying for a rental flat and starting work again.

sections.label: MP's 20 letters, no answer
sections.summary: Her sympathetic MP advocates for her, but after 20 letters and hours of MPS sessions, no one knows why an exception cannot be made.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Her sympathetic MP advocates for her but after 20 letters back and forth, back and forth, and hours of Meet-the-People (MPS) sessions, no one is any wiser, not even her MP, about why an exception cannot be made for her case.

sections.label: Higher taxes and trust
sections.summary: If higher taxes are needed someday, the speaker thinks many Singaporeans will accept it, but trust must be very high and taxpayers honestly engaged.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If there is a need to pay higher taxes someday, as the Minister hinted, in order to build a better system that moves everyone forward together, I think many Singaporeans will be prepared to bite that bullet because we are a far more generous people than we give ourselves credit for.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Trust has to be very high for that to happen.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I believe there are many taxpayers and voters on the ground who will still need to be more honestly engaged and deeply convinced that this system's story is genuinely about moving everyone forward together and not just moving some of us forward together.

sections.label: Hard questions on policies
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether mandatory off-days, ending early streaming and more generous welfare would really cause the feared collapses, noting some Singaporeans have reached breaking points.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Is it really true that once we give mandatory off-days to our foreign domestic workers, we will see the instant collapse of our work-life balance?

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Is it for real that if we free our children from the tyranny of early streaming and high-stakes exams, we will see our future workforce become that much less rigorous?

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Is it for certain that if we uplift our poorest through more generous welfare, we will see the decimation of Singapore's culture of hard work?

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There are Singaporeans out there who ask hard questions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There are Singaporeans out there who even live out their hard answers to those hard questions, and some of them are still here, still open, still pushing the boundaries, but some of them have already reached their breaking points where they have decided they are done with this city.

sections.label: Budget help for the needy
sections.summary: A Member hopes each Budget brings more help and hope to those who need it most, noting an overall surplus of $1.9 billion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It has always needed every one of us, perhaps more than we will ever know.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But allow me also the space to hope that each new Budget you bring will be one that finds new ways to bring ever more help and ever more hope to the drowning ones and the ones in the basement that need it most, because this is their city, too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: I am sure many Members have the same experience which you have just shared with us.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It is reassuring to know that we will have an overall surplus of $1.9 billion, even though we are running an expansionary Budget.

sections.label: Water price increase concerns
sections.summary: The impending 30% water price increase has dominated ground discussions, with residents and businesses surprised and worried about the impact.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Much is at stake as our economy moves into a higher gear.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, the impending 30% water price increase has dominated most of the discussions on the ground instead.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Residents and businesses alike were taken by surprise − "why so much so suddenly" − and worried about the impact from such a big hike.

sections.label: Rental rebates for hawkers
sections.summary: A Member appeals for rental rebates for hawkers and stallholders facing higher water bills, later electricity price hikes and rising food prices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: While the increase in water prices should not lead to drastic increases in the prices of our food, I still see the need to appeal for rental rebates for our hawkers and stallholders who will have to incur higher costs due to higher water bills and, later on, electricity price hikes from the carbon tax, on top of a rising trend in food prices.

sections.label: MRT doors open longer
sections.summary: A Member asks whether MRT doors could stay open longer during off-peak periods at stations with more seniors, such as Outram.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Would it be possible for our MRT doors to stay open for a little longer during off-peak periods at stations where there are more seniors, for example, at Outram station which serves the Singapore General Hospital?

sections.label: Childcare centres convertible to eldercare
sections.summary: A Member suggests childcare centres in maturing estates be convertible into eldercare centres, and new ones designed to accommodate such changes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For example, we build childcare centres to cater to children but, with shrinking family sizes and an ageing population, the childcare centres located in the older maturing estates which may experience falling enrolment in the future should be convertible into eldercare centres.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This way, the Government will not have to look for a new space, nor incur heavy building expenses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Hence, when building new childcare centres, the Government should also consider that the design can accommodate changes to eldercare centres in the longer term.

sections.label: Motivating elderly for courses
sections.summary: A Member hopes the Government studies what motivates local elderly and supports recruiting retirees for the care sector with subsidised training.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: How do we motivate them and get them excited about trying out new things?

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I hope the Government will conduct a study into the psyche of our local elderly to find what motivates them so that we can use the information to formulate attractive ways to run our courses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It would also be helpful if the Government can support the recruitment of retirees for the care sector with subsidised training and training allowances.

sections.label: Partnerships for ageing population care
sections.summary: The speaker suggests Grab, Uber and the Agency for Integrated Care work together to use spare capacity, and proposes action on ageing care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Grab and Uber should likewise consider doing so, and the Agency for Integrated Care can work with these car hiring companies to make good use of their spare capacities, instead of relying solely on ambulances.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Finance Minister struck a chord with me when he said, "We need to foster partnerships in the wider society so we can maintain a good balance between state action and community initiative".

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Budget 2017 will outline measures for our economy and our society." Today, I would like to base the rest of my speech on the above points concerning our society.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I was most heartened when the Finance Minister said that: "We are building an inclusive and caring society − one where Singaporeans of all backgrounds can improve their lives, where the vulnerable are uplifted, and where people of all ages can look to the future with optimism." I want to suggest the following action to reposition Singapore for better care of our ageing population.

sections.label: Rising elderly healthcare spending
sections.summary: Healthcare spending doubled to about $10 billion in FY2016, and elderly healthcare costs are projected to exceed $66 billion annually within 15 years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Finance Minister said that over the last five years, our annual healthcare spending has more than doubled to around $10 billion in financial year 2016.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Elderly healthcare costs here are projected to rise 10 times over the next 15 years to more than $66 billion annually.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This means an average of $45,000 will be spent on healthcare for each senior by 2030.

sections.label: Seniors living alone
sections.summary: About 7% of seniors over 65, or 35,000, lived alone in 2012, projected to reach about 90,000 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In 2012, about 7% of seniors older than 65, or 35,000 seniors, live alone.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This will go up to about 90,000 by 2030.

sections.label: Aged care capacity and support ratio
sections.summary: About 5% of seniors live in residential aged care, and Singapore's old age support ratio is expected to fall to 2.3 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Presently, about 5% of seniors live in some form of residential aged care facility and this will translate to about 50,000 of seniors requiring assisted living by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Despite a 30% increase in capacity since 2010, Singapore still had fewer nursing home beds per 1,000 people aged 65 and above in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Singapore's old age support ratio has been dropping from 7.4 in 2010 to 5.4 in 2016 and is expected to drop to 2.3 by 2030.

sections.label: Layoffs late last year
sections.summary: The passage states that several layoffs late last year accounted for more than 10,000 jobs lost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If my facts are right, there were several layoffs late last year which account to more than 10,000 jobs being lost.

sections.label: Family dysfunction and financial instability
sections.summary: An AMP study then showed a strong correlation between dysfunctional families and the financial instability of the family.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A study made by AMP then showed a strong correlation between dysfunctional families and the financial instability of the family.

sections.label: Economy and PMET layoffs
sections.summary: The economy's downward trend is expected to continue in 2017 and 2018, possibly causing more layoffs and retrenchments, especially affecting PMETs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In my view, the worrying downward trend of the economy is expected not to get any better in 2017 and 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If this trend prevails, more job layoffs and retrenchments may occur, especially affecting the professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs).

sections.label: Outsourcing MOM engagement work
sections.summary: It asks whether some of MOM's work engaging outplaced individuals can be outsourced to Malay/Muslim Organisations or self-help groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can some of the work done by MOM in engaging the outplaced individuals be "outsourced" and handled and managed by some of the credible Malay/Muslim Organisations (MMOs) or even self-help groups (SHGs)?

sections.label: Budget, SMEs and retrenchments
sections.summary: It states the Budget aims to ensure job security by assisting SMEs and preparing for long-term challenges, and that retrenchments will still occur if the situation persists.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is with the belief that we should thwart future potential social problems by ensuring that our affected workers are unperturbed by the disruption in their job, leading to a stable financial position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is a noteworthy Budget that aims to ensure job security for Singaporeans by proposing measures to assist the smaller firms (SMEs) and preparing our country for challenges in the long term, in line with the recommendations by CFE.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If this situation persists, I am certain that retrenchments will still occur, similar to what we have witnessed in 2016.

sections.label: Malay/Muslim bodies helping jobless
sections.summary: Fewer affected Malay/Muslim individuals sought MOM's help than other races, so action should not be by MOM solely but also mobilise AMP, MENDAKI, PPIS and Jamiyah.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Although MOM provides various schemes and programmes, it was found that not many affected Malay/Muslim individuals sought MOM's help as compared to the other races.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, I would like to suggest that action should not be undertaken by MOM solely and, in fact, we should also mobilise the efforts of major Malay/Muslim bodies like AMP, MENDAKI, PPIS and Jamiyah.

sections.label: Funding self-help groups' MOM role
sections.summary: It says the groups' involvement with MOM as an agent to engage jobless individuals is important, and hopes the Finance Ministry provides financial help and funds to self-help groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Their involvement with MOM, in order to facilitate as an agent for MOM, to engage individuals who have lost their jobs and get back into the workforce is so important, in my opinion, which will help the country to avoid long-term social issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope the Finance Ministry can look into this and provide the necessary financial help and funds to the self-help groups in order to be able to make this a success.

sections.label: Transport, healthcare and Silver Support
sections.summary: It cites Minister Heng on over $20 billion for public transport over five years, healthcare spending doubling to around $10 billion yearly, and Silver Support giving up to $750 every three months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Minister Heng mentioned that additional investment in our public transport infrastructure is expected to cost the Government more than $20 billion over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Our annual healthcare spending has more than doubled over the past five years to around $10 billion a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For instance, the Silver Support Scheme, which gives up to $750 every three months to the elderly, has really helped reduce hardship for some of our most vulnerable elderly staying in 1- to 2-room flats.

sections.label: Private residential price decline
sections.summary: Private residential prices in Singapore have fallen for 13 straight quarters, dropping 3% last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Private residential prices in Singapore have slipped for 13th straight quarters and have fallen by 3% last year.

sections.label: Buyer's Stamp Duty rates
sections.summary: The Buyer's Stamp Duty rate is 1% for the first $180,000 and 2% for the next $180,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Buyer's Stamp Duty rate for the first $180,000 is 1%, followed by 2% for the next $180,000.

sections.label: Support for Budget initiatives
sections.summary: The speaker supports Budget initiatives including digitalisation for SMEs, the International Partnership Fund and public sector productivity funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I speak in support of the Government's Budget and its various initiatives that I believe are necessary in these uncertain times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They include: the promotion of digitalisation for Small and Medium Enterprises, the International Partnership Fund that encourages companies to internationalise, as well as the various public sector productivity funds that encourage innovation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These are all measures that will be crucial for businesses that need to dial up their innovation in the face of ever-faster disruptions arising from technological advances.

sections.label: Singapore Kindness Movement speech
sections.summary: In May 2007 Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong said social development must complement building a vibrant global city.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Ten years ago, in May 2007, Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong gave a speech at the 10th anniversary of the Singapore Kindness Movement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: He said, and I quote, that our efforts to build a vibrant, global city "will be in vain unless we complement them with social development, to build a Singapore with a heart.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As we grow and globalise, the values of care, compassion and neighbourliness will become even more important." Mdm Speaker, Singaporeans have been trying to be a kinder people − at least officially − for the past 20 years.

sections.label: Ageing Singaporeans and employers
sections.summary: By 2030 one in five Singaporeans will be 65 and above, and employers seem to favour the young for lower wages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By 2030, one in every five Singaporeans will be aged 65 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While the Government has done a tremendous amount of work in drafting legislation and schemes that protect the rights of the elderly and promote re-employment, more can be done to ensure that the elderly remain as a core driving force of our economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The challenge we see in industry is a worrying trend of employers who seem to favour the young because of lower wages.

sections.label: External vendors for position
sections.summary: It was cheaper for the company to use external vendors for his position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, it was cheaper for the company to use external vendors for his position.

sections.label: Valuing age and experience
sections.summary: Age, experience and credibility should be treasured, celebrated, embraced and rewarded, especially amid fake news and alternative reality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Instead, age, experience and credibility should be treasured, celebrated and embraced, somewhat like fine wine, and rewarded accordingly, particularly in this era of "fake news" and "alternative reality".

sections.label: Terrex vehicles detained in Hong Kong
sections.summary: Social media spread conspiracy theories over Terrex vehicles detained in Hong Kong; the speaker commends the Government's measured handling and the vehicles' return.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Take the recent example of the Singapore Armed Forces Terrex vehicles that were detained in Hong Kong.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Social media was rife with callous and irresponsible conspiracy theories and conjecture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In my humble opinion, I felt that the Government's approach and handling of this delicate situation was spot on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I commend Minister for Foreign Affairs Vivian Balakrishnan and Minister for Defence Ng Eng Hen for their gracious and measured approach on this issue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And after a few weeks, we got our tanks back, safe and sound.

sections.label: Empathy in polarised world
sections.summary: In a fragmented world celebrating alternative facts and fake news, people should foster a caring, inclusive society through empathy and grace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this fragmented, polarised world where "alternative facts" and "fake news" are celebrated and validated, it is all the more important that we work together to foster a more caring and inclusive society by exercising empathy and grace.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Besides the quantum of the increase, what shook people were the suddenness of the announcement and the very short lead time from the announcement in February to its implementation in July.

sections.label: Carbon tax two-year lead time
sections.summary: There is a two-year lead time for the impending carbon tax, announced ahead of its 2019 implementation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: By contrast, there is a two-year lead time for the impending carbon tax, which the Government is announcing ahead of its implementation in 2019.

sections.label: KPMG survey on PIC use
sections.summary: In a 2014 post-Budget KPMG survey, 58% of 80 senior executives admitted using the PIC to defray operating expenses rather than raise productivity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, in 2014, a post-Budget survey conducted by KPMG, 58% of the 80 senior executives surveyed admitted using the PIC to defray operating expenses, instead of using it to raise productivity.

sections.label: Productivity growth target
sections.summary: The aim was to grow productivity by 2% to 3% yearly over a decade, reaching a 30% increase by 2019.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The aim was to grow productivity by 2% to 3% per year over a decade, which should bring us to a 30% productivity increase by 2019.

sections.label: Revised land sales figures
sections.summary: The revised land sales figure for this Financial Year is $11.8 billion and the projection for the coming Financial Year is $8.2 billion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Today, we see the revised land sales figure for this Financial Year to be $11.8 billion and the projection for the coming Financial Year to be $8.2 billion.

sections.label: Reviewing spending and revenue sources
sections.summary: Questions are whether past and current initiatives were reviewed to weed out wasteful expenditures and whether revenue sources were completely recognised.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The legitimate questions being asked are whether we have done adequate reviews of past and current initiatives to weed out wasteful and ineffective expenditures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The other issue is whether we have completely recognised our sources of revenue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Doing so will help to ensure that we do not place unnecessary tax burdens on the people.

sections.label: Social mobility and HDB grants
sections.summary: The passage calls for continuing social mobility, providing opportunities, and supporting increased grants on resale HDB flats for young couples.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Next, the need to continue progressing on the path of social mobility and providing Singaporeans with opportunities and, finally, to accord strong support for the increased grants on resale HDB flats as they will provide young couples with the real possibility of owning a more affordable first property more quickly.

sections.label: Australia training land deal
sections.summary: An enhanced deal with Australia was signed for land to train 14,000 personnel for 18 weeks per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: A key highlight last year was the signing of an enhanced deal with Australia for a piece of land to train 14,000 personnel for 18 weeks per year.

sections.label: Keppel cuts capacity and jobs
sections.summary: Keppel cut yard capacity by two overseas and three in Singapore and cut 10,600 jobs from its Offshore and Marine division.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In fact, Keppel, one of the largest oil-rig builders in the world, cut its yard capacity − two overseas and three in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It had also cut 10,600 jobs from its Offshore and Marine division last year.

sections.label: Adapt and Grow Initiative
sections.summary: The enhanced Adapt and Grow Initiative, including Attach and Train, gives participants work attachment opportunities, benefiting employees and employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This allows the worker to plan longer term − in terms of the housing, educational and fiscal needs of his family.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This is why the Adapt and Grow Initiative, which has been enhanced to include Attach and Train, is key in the present economic climate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)

sections.label: Budget as rallying call

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)

sections.label: Job market insecurity and productivity

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As it is well known, productivity performance in recent times has been poor and far below our target.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)

sections.label: Academic testing and entrepreneurship

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)

sections.label: Budget innovation digital economy

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
