sections.summary: The passage applauds the Finance Minister for signalling fiscal prudence through a permanent 2% downward adjustment from the budget caps of all Ministries and Organs of State.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: On expenditure front, I applaud the Finance Minister for sending out a strong signal of fiscal prudence, with the permanent 2% downward adjustment from the budget caps of all Ministries and Organs of State.

sections.label: Vacant Government properties
sections.summary: The passage states that a recent Parliamentary Question indicates as many as 1,000 Government properties are vacant, pending lease, redevelopment or demolition, some for extended periods.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: From a recent Parliamentary Question, I understand there are as many as 1,000 Government properties that are vacant, pending lease, redevelopment or demolition, some of which stay vacant for extended periods of time.

sections.label: Short-term help for retrenched workers
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Government to consider suspending retrenched workers' income tax instalments and allowing flexible CPF use for mortgages during unemployment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Whilst I appreciate that Adapt and Grow has launched an extensive set of programmes to help workers take on new jobs, I call on the Government to consider some short-term measures to help families cope during this transition.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: For example, during periods of unemployment, would the Government consider suspending the retrenched workers' payment of income tax instalments and allow some flexible use of CPF to pay mortgages, so as to help them keep their homes?

sections.label: SkillsFuture and inclusive approach
sections.summary: Singapore launched SkillsFuture nationwide in 2014, and the speaker says the approach must be inclusive, noting some jobless may have found relief as Uber drivers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Singapore had the foresight to launch the SkillsFuture movement nationwide in 2014 as our next wave of development, and we must make sure our approach is an inclusive one, benefiting all Singaporeans along the journey.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Some of those who lost their jobs may have found relief as Uber drivers − itself a fortuitous result of industry disruption − but I fear this too could be a short-lived job, with the advancement of self-driving technologies.

sections.label: Water tariff increase and tax
sections.summary: The Budget announced a 30% rise in water tariffs and a water consumption tax, which left many Singaporeans anxious.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: First of all, the increase of water tariffs by 30% and the imposition of water consumption tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In this year's Budget, the announcement by Finance Minister to raise water tariffs by 30% left many Singaporeans anxious.

sections.label: Rebates and affected users
sections.summary: The Government will give rebates to some families through GST vouchers and U-Save rebates, but most Singaporeans and industrial/commercial users will be affected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Although the Government has said that it will be giving rebates to some families through GST vouchers U-Save rebates, most Singaporeans and industrial/commercial users will be affected, as they do not fulfil the criteria to enjoy rebates or will be receiving only token rebates.

sections.label: Diesel tax increase
sections.summary: The speaker is concerned about a 10 cents per litre increase in diesel tax applying to car diesel, industrial diesel and bio-diesel.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Second, I am also very concerned about the increase in diesel tax by 10 cents per litre, which applies to car diesel, industrial diesel and bio-diesel.

sections.label: Taxis and diesel tax savings
sections.summary: Even if taxi companies returned $850 in savings from the reduced special diesel tax to drivers, drivers would still need cash to cover higher diesel prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For taxis, even if taxi companies were to return the savings of $850 from the reduced special diesel tax to taxi drivers, the taxi drivers would still have to come up with cash to make up for the increase in diesel prices.

sections.label: Safeguarding Singaporean employment
sections.summary: The passage states that economic headwinds and strategic challenges require continuing to safeguard Singaporeans' employment by creating good jobs and helping the economy transit to its next phase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In view of these economic headwinds and strategic challenges, we must continue to safeguard the employment of Singaporeans by creating good jobs and by helping our economy transit into the next phase.

sections.label: Strategic Budget amid global uncertainty
sections.summary: The passage states this year's Budget is strategic, aiming to help Singapore grow despite global uncertainty, and shifts from intensive-driven to strategies-driven approaches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I believe that we use this time to focus, we use this time to regroup, we plan our strategy and we move forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, this year's Budget is really a strategic one that aims to help Singapore grow despite this global uncertainty that we are living in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The shift from the traditional intensive-driven Budget to the current strategies-driven one demonstrates the Government's appreciation that Singapore's economy is, indeed, becoming increasingly more complex and intertwined with the rest of the world.

sections.label: SME digitalisation assistance
sections.summary: The passage states SMEs cannot assume they can keep operating as before, and Industry Digital Plans and the SME Technology Hub will provide baseline assistance to digitalise their businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While it is unlikely that digital platforms and online business models will completely supplant traditional modes of business, our SMEs cannot afford to assume that they can continue to operate the way that they have been operating.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, the implementation of the Industry Digital Plans and the setting up of the SME Technology Hub will provide our SMEs with the much needed baseline assistance to digitalise their businesses, and I am eager to hear more details from the Ministry of Communications and Information during the committee of Supply debate.

sections.label: International Partnership Fund for SMEs
sections.summary: The passage states the International Partnership Fund proposed in the Budget will help catalyse the regionalisation of Singapore's SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The International Partnership Fund proposed in the Budget will help catalyse the regionalisation of our SMEs.

sections.label: CPF housing grant structure
sections.summary: The passage states current CPF housing grants for 4- and 5-room flats are similar at $30,000, but the new structure would give 4-room flat buyers a higher grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The current CPF housing grants for both 4- and 5-room flats are similar at $30,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The new grant structure, however, would provide those who purchase a 4-room flat a higher grant than those who purchase a 5-room flat.

sections.label: Percentage-based housing grant proposal
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government would consider a percentage-grant based on flat purchase price, subject to an absolute ceiling, with the higher amount given to qualifying purchasers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In view of these idiosyncrasies, would the Government consider providing a percentage-grant based on the purchase price of the flat?

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: But this amount would be subject to an absolute ceiling amount, and whichever amount is then higher would be given to the qualifying purchaser as the housing grant.

sections.label: Uneven growth impact across sectors
sections.summary: Singapore's modest GDP growth and 2.6% annual real median wage growth from 2009 to 2016 were not felt equally across all sectors and society strata.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Although Singapore has experienced modest GDP growth over the past few years with real median wage growing by 2.6% per annum, from 2009 to 2016, the impact of these growth figures has not be felt equally across all sectors of the economy and strata of the society.

sections.label: Extending SME Working Capital Loan
sections.summary: A suggestion that the Government consider extending the SME Working Capital Loan to let SMEs collateralise receivables owed by big companies for low-interest loans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: First, I wonder if the Government could consider extending the scope of the SME Working Capital Loan, under which the Government assumes the risk for loan defaults, to allow SMEs to collateralise their receivables owed by big companies for loans at low interest rates.

sections.label: Extending BCA Security of Payment Act
sections.summary: A suggestion that the BCA Security of Payment Act framework, allowing employers to pay subcontractors directly, be extended to other industries with multi-tiered relationships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Second, I suggest that the framework in the BCA Security of Payment Act for the building and construction industry, which allows the employer to make payments directly to a subcontractor when the main contractor fails to do so, be extended to other industries where such multi-tiered relationships also exist.

sections.label: Wage Credit Scheme co-funding extension
sections.summary: The Scheme has the Government co-fund 40% of wage increases for Singaporean employees earning gross monthly salaries of $4,000 and below, and is extended by two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Under this Scheme, the Government co-funds 40% of wage increases for Singaporean employees earning gross monthly salaries of $4,000, which is roughly about the 50th percentile of wages in Singapore, and below.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This Scheme is extended by two years under the Government's plan to continue supporting businesses.

sections.label: Speeding up carbon tax consultations
sections.summary: A suggestion that consultations be speeded up and a decision made as soon as practicable on the carbon tax rate, implementation schedule and transition measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For the above reasons, I respectfully suggest that the consultations be speeded up and a decision be made as soon as practicable on the precise carbon tax rate, the implementation schedule and the measures to ease the transition for affected companies.

sections.label: Wage Credit Scheme funding and skills
sections.summary: $600 million is set aside for the Wage Credit Scheme for wage rises for Singaporeans, with investment in skills, partnerships and digitalisation opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Just for an example, $600 million is being set aside for the Wage Credit Scheme to allow companies to use this Scheme to pay wage rises for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In particular, the serious investment in relation to helping Singaporeans deepen their skills, companies to deepen their partnerships, and to basically look out for opportunities in the digitalisation space.

sections.label: Economy growth and CFE forecast
sections.summary: The economy grew 2% last year with growth picking up in the final quarter, and the CFE expects 2% to 3% annual growth over the next decade.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Last year our economy grew at 2%, with growth picking up in the final quarter.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The CFE expects annual growth of 2% to 3% over the next decade.

sections.label: ASEAN, China, India growth
sections.summary: ASEAN, China and India are bright spots, with ASEAN-5 expected to grow 4.9% this year, China about 6.7% and India about 6.6%.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), China and India are bright spots, with the ASEAN-5 countries expected to grow at 4.9% this year, China at about 6.7% and India at about 6.6%.

sections.label: McKinsey emerging Asia infrastructure demand
sections.summary: McKinsey estimates infrastructure demand in emerging Asian markets, particularly China, Southeast Asia and South Asia, will grow by about US$20 trillion between 2016 and 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: McKinsey estimates that the demand for infrastructure in emerging Asian markets, particularly China, Southeast Asia and South Asia, will grow by about US$20 trillion between 2016 and 2030.

sections.label: International Finance Scheme extension
sections.summary: A key initiative in this Budget is the extension of the International Finance Scheme to Non-Recourse Financing.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In this Budget, a key initiative is really the extension of our International Finance Scheme to Non-Recourse Financing.

sections.label: International Partnership Fund
sections.summary: This Budget specifically includes a $600 million International Partnership Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In this Budget specifically, there is a $600 million International Partnership Fund.

sections.label: Government loan programmes
sections.summary: The Government has a suite of loan programmes that will collectively catalyse $5 billion in loans up to 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The Government has a suite of loan programmes which will collectively catalyse $5 billion in loans up to 2020.

sections.label: Internationalisation Finance Scheme for SMEs
sections.summary: The Budget announced the Internationalisation Finance Scheme for Non-Recourse Financing to help SMEs participate in opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In this Budget, the specific announcement was on the Internationalisation Finance Scheme for Non-Recourse Financing to help SMEs participate in these opportunities.

sections.label: Catalysing loans for infrastructure projects
sections.summary: Over five years, $600 million in loans is expected to be catalysed, corresponding to about $1 billion in infrastructure projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Over the next five years, we expect to catalyse $600 million dollars in loans, which will probably correspond to about $1 billion in infrastructure projects.

sections.label: SME intellectual property commercialisation funding
sections.summary: SMEs are helped to commercialise intellectual property through Centres of Innovation, with about $100 million committed.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: One is to help SMEs commercialise intellectual property through our network of Centres of Innovation, and a substantial amount of funding has been committed, about $100 million for this.

sections.label: Headstart Programme IP licence extension
sections.summary: The Headstart Programme lets A*STAR give SMEs royalty-free exclusive IP licences, now extended from 18 to 36 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The Headstart Programme, where A*STAR allows SMEs to enjoy royalty-free and exclusive IP licences for up to 18 months until recently.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: With this Budget, it has now gone up to 36 months.

sections.label: Grant support for SME capability development
sections.summary: In total, about $1.5 billion of grant support exists for capability development of SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In total, we have about $1.5 billion of grant support for such capability development of SMEs.

sections.label: Making Government support accessible to SMEs
sections.summary: Agencies worked to make Government support more accessible to SMEs through the Business Grants Portal, SME Digital Technology Hub and Intellectual Property Master Agreement.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Even on that score, our agencies have worked on how we can make Government support more accessible to SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, they have got the Business Grants Portal, SME Digital Technology Hub and the new Intellectual Property Master Agreement.

sections.label: Container Depot Association electronic trucking
sections.summary: CDAS has been involved in launching an electronic container trucking system to track truck movement and enhance supply chain efficiencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Container Depot Association (Singapore), or CDAS − probably not something that many Members are familiar with.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: But they have been involved in a major effort in terms of launching electronic container trucking system and they want to track the movement of their trucks, and it is going to enhance their supply chain and how they introduce efficiencies and the way they deploy their fleet and so on.

sections.label: Sector growth and contraction
sections.summary: Electronics grew 15% last year, transport and storage grew 2.3%, and marine and offshore engineering contracted for nine successive quarters.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: You have sectors like electronics that grew at 15% last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: You have a sector like transport and storage that grew by 2.3% last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: You have a sector like marine and offshore engineering that has contracted for nine successive quarters.

sections.label: Cash pay-outs and SME loans
sections.summary: About $1 billion in cash pay-outs went to businesses in March, and the 2016 SME Working Capital Loan catalysed about $700 million in loans to about 4,300 SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Collectively, this is about $1 billion in cash pay-outs to businesses in March this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: It is a significant outlay from the Government to alleviate some of the cost pressure on our businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Also, in terms of liquidity, we have introduced the SME Working Capital Loan in 2016, which has basically catalysed about $700 million in loans to about 4,300 SMEs.

sections.label: Government support for SME transitions
sections.summary: The Government supports SMEs through broad-based and targeted programmes, focusing on SMEs and working with trade associations, chambers and unions.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: As for the Government, we are resolute in our support, through broad-based and targeted programmes, to help our SMEs make the transition successful.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: We do not engage in the art, or perhaps, Mr Perera thinks it is the science of picking winners, but we will support companies that are prepared to make these important transitions because they see the benefit and they are prepared to take the important steps to move the organisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In all of these efforts, the SMEs would be our central focus.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Ultimately, creating a vibrant, competitive industry with strong capabilities is the surest way of ensuring success of all our businesses, including the SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And so, we look forward to working closely with the trade associations and chambers, and the unions to ensure that we have a diverse enterprise eco-system, from startups to SMEs, to large local enterprises, to multi-nationals − we have a thriving SME community, and an economy that is rich with opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This increase comes on the back of a 15%-odd increase in HDB car park charges, higher electricity and gas charges and the announcement of higher S&CC all in the space of about three months.

sections.label: 1997 water price increase
sections.summary: When water prices were last raised in 1997, they rose 120% for households and 30% for industrial and commercial users over four years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The last time an announcement was made to raise water prices in 1997, prices were raised by 120% for households and 30% for industrial and commercial users over a four-year period.

sections.label: NEWater production cost reduction
sections.summary: PUB brought down NEWater production cost from $1.30 to $1.15 per cubic metre from 2002 to 2004 through more competitive membrane technologies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If this is so, what are the projections for expected water price hikes as the population grows?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is noteworthy, Mr Deputy Speaker, that the PUB was able to bring down the cost of NEWater production from 2002 to 2004 from $1.30 to $1.15 per cubic metre as a result of more competitive membrane technologies.

sections.label: Sembcorp NEWater plant bid price
sections.summary: In 2008 Sembcorp won the bid for the fifth and largest NEWater plant and submitted a first-year price of about $0.30 per cubic metre.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2008, Sembcorp, which secured the bid to design, build, own and operate the fifth and largest NEWater plant, submitted a first-year price of about $0.30 to produce a cubic metre of NEWater.

sections.label: Linggui Reservoir water levels and abstraction
sections.summary: Water levels were 84% in 2015, 49% in 2016 and 27% in 2017, and the passage asks how often Singapore drew less than 250 million gallons a day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At the start of each respective year, the water levels were at 84% in 2015, 49% in 2016 and 27% in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We have been informed by the Minister of Foreign Affairs in response to a Parliamentary Question in January this year that there is a significant risk of the water levels in the Linggui Reservoir falling to 0% this year should there be a dry spell in Johor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In view of the low water levels in the Linggui Reservoir from 2015 onwards in particular, how often has Singapore drawn less than the 250 million gallons a day it is legally entitled to under the 1962 Water Agreement and what has been Singapore's average daily rate of abstraction from the Linggui Reservoir since 2014?

sections.label: Two Johor water transfer proposals
sections.summary: The first proposal was a low wall channelling about 50mgd from the Sayong River catchment at about RM$250 million, and the second a dam at Ulu Sedili Besar River transferring about 110mgd at RM$660 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The first proposal was to build a low wall to channel about 50mgd of water from the Sayong River catchment area at the cost of about RM$250 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The second plan called for the building of a dam at the Ulu Sedili Besar River to transfer about 110mgd to the Johor River at the cost of RM$660 million.

sections.label: Singapore per capita water consumption decline
sections.summary: Singapore's per capita water consumption dropped from 162 litres per day in 2005 to 151 litres per day today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In fact, Singapore's per capita water consumption rates have been dropping steadily from 2005 when it was 162 litres per day to 151 litres per day today.

sections.label: Water conservation tax differentiation proposal
sections.summary: The passage proposes differentiating water conservation tax by usage, keeping it at 30% for a four-person household at the national average, instead of the Budget's blunt increases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What may truly push a renewed commitment to a water conservation drive is to significantly alter a consumer behaviour towards a tax regime that differentiates between efficient and inefficient usage of water by lowering taxes for consumers who use less water.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, a household of four which meets the national average consumption can have their water conservation tax remain at the current 30% of the tariff rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Depending on additional usage, PUB could establish an ascending or descending scale relative to consumption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This has better prospects for water conservation as real savings would be given to individual households, building on the current two-tiered approach between households that consume more or less than 40 cubic meters of waters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This approach would also be more targeted and would cohere with the objective of saving water as opposed to the Budget announcement which bluntly increases the water conservation tax from 30% to 50%, and 35% to 65% for all households.

sections.label: Call for explanation of water pricing
sections.summary: The passage calls for a deeper Government explanation of water pricing and long-run cost imperatives, noting the hike followed other municipal price increases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I believe a deeper explanation from the Government about how it prices water and its long-run cost imperatives would enable the public to better understand and rationalise this water hike in addition to improving public understanding on this issue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This would be important as the water price hike occurred on the back of many other municipal prices increases which could arguably have been better phased to reduce the impact on the average Singaporean for whom cost of living concerns are an increasing issue.

sections.label: Tracking SME growth and funding
sections.summary: A Member asks whether the Government tracks SMEs that grow into global companies and whether poor results justify more interventionist funding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: If you want to raise a clarification about the Minister's speech, raise the clarification but do not make another speech, please.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: So, my clarificatory point would be: does the Government actually track how many SMEs take advantage of these schemes and grow, and stop becoming SMEs and actually become global companies?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: And if in fact those results are tracked and those results are not good, then would that not suggest that there is a role for the Government to take a more active stance in grooming these companies?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Because I certainly do hear feedback that the funding needs are not fully met.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: And would the Minister not acknowledge that if so, would there not be a role for the Government to actually be more interventionist to provide funding at higher levels of caps for those SMEs which have self-selected themselves by demonstrating a track record of results as opposed to SMEs who remain SMEs for decades.

sections.label: Phasing out of schemes
sections.summary: Some schemes will be phased out in future, as the Productivity and Innovation Credit is being tapered down.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Some of these schemes will be phased out in the future, in the way that the Productivity and Innovation Credit (PIC) is being tapered down, for example.

sections.label: Structural impediments to entrepreneurship
sections.summary: A Member asks what the Government's strategy is to address fundamental structural impediments to entrepreneurship, citing land cost, funding and culture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: It is in that context that I raised land cost, funding and the overall culture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: So, what would be the Government's strategy to address that fundamental structural impediment to entrepreneurship?

sections.label: Goal of 1,000 companies
sections.summary: The Economic Review Committee set a goal of 1,000 companies crossing $100-million turnover by the end of the decade, which is monitored and on track.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: As for the rate at which we get globally competitive companies, if I may draw Members' attention, in the Economic Review Committee report, there was a goal to have 1,000 companies that cross the $100-million turnover mark by the end of this decade.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: That was an important directional goal because it is to set a sense of the scale of ambition that we have, and it is something that we continue to monitor.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I would say that on balance, we are on track to getting there.

sections.label: Guarantees and scheme consultation
sections.summary: Personal and corporate guarantees shackle smaller companies, so a scheme was introduced after consulting banks, industry and companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, the easy way out when you are dealing with smaller companies, or the one way to mitigate the risk, is to say I need personal guarantees and corporate guarantees, which immediately shackles the company in terms of how far it can go.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, we have tried to come in with this scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: This is after consultation with all the key players − the banks, the industry, companies and so on.

sections.label: Speech on Budget impact
sections.summary: The Member's speech will focus on the Budget's economic transformation aspects and its impact on mature workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: For me, my speech today will focus on the economic transformation aspects of the Budget and on the impact on mature workers.

sections.label: ITMs, CFE funding, partnership capability
sections.summary: Speaker supports Budget's $2.4 billion CFE funding and stresses implementing ITMs and building leadership and partnership capability in trade associations and tripartite partners.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In other words, it is akin to moving from being a chess piece to being a chess player, and a strong one.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Therefore, even as I support and commend this year's Budget for adding another $2.4 billion in CFE-related funding over the coming four years on top of the $4.5 billion that was already set aside in last year's Budget for the Industry Transformation Programme, I want to emphasise the importance of implementing the ITMs and in building leadership and partnership reflexes and capability in the trade associations and chambers, and the tripartite partners.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: This is because ITMs, whatever their details, will begin to be outdated the moment they are defined.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Therefore, we must not delude ourselves into believing that submitting or approving a ITM, or even in implementing fully an approved ITM, would suffice.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In a sense, we have to complement once-in-seven or 10-year economic committees such as the Economic Review Committee or the CFE with a decentralised yet capably led, continuously adaptive, responsive, innovative partnership structure that is alive and that goes on all the time, with all the partners that I have mentioned drawing upon all the resources there are.

sections.label: Mature workers' job security worries
sections.summary: Mature workers welcome the re-employment age ceiling rising from 65 to 67 from July, but many worry about job security.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Even though mature workers welcome the raising of the re-employment age ceiling from 65 to 67 that will happen from July this year, many are worried about their job security.

sections.label: Wage subsidies for mature workers
sections.summary: Tripartite partners agreed mature workers are not to be targeted for discriminatory retrenchment, and extended wage subsidies help address cost differentials.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The tripartite partners have long agreed that mature workers, including re-employed workers, are not to be targeted for discriminatory retrenchment or termination.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: On the Government's part, the extension of the Special Employment Credit and the Additional Special Employment Credit, being wage subsidies to companies to lower the cost of employing mature workers, will help address cost differentials between older and younger workers in the same jobs, and in this period, particularly pertinent.

sections.label: Extension benefits 120,000 workers
sections.summary: The extension benefits about 120,000 workers and 55,000 employers at a cost of about $160 million, with support of up to 11% of wages.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The extension will benefit about 120,000 workers and 55,000 employers, at a cost of about $160 million.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Taken together with the Special Employment Credit, employers will receive support of up to 11% for the wages of their eligible older workers", This wage subsidy for mature workers in a slower economy helps boost their cost-competitiveness, and the Labour Movement is grateful to Government for that.

sections.label: HR profession and experienced workers
sections.summary: Speaker urges the HR profession to adopt HR Sectoral Tripartite Committee recommendations and MOM's Human Capital Programme initiatives to maximise human capital contribution.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: So, please do not under-estimate the value of an experienced worker.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: This is also a time and opportunity for the human resources (HR) profession to step up and help companies maximise the contribution of their human capital, beyond just making tactical moves.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In this regard, I urge the HR profession to pro-actively and seriously support and adopt the recommendations of the HR Sectoral Tripartite Committee and initiatives under the MOM's Human Capital Programme.

sections.label: Water bill increases and rebates
sections.summary: PUB analysis says 1- to 2-room HDB households see no water bill increase after U-Save rebates, 4-room flats see $5 more monthly, and 75% of shop owners see $25 more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: According to PUB's analysis, Singaporeans living in 1- to 2-room HDB flat will not see any increase in their water bill after factoring the U-Save rebates, while Singaporeans living in 4-room HDB flats will only see a small increase of $5 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: For 75% of shop owners, they will only see an increase of $25 in their monthly water bill after tariffs go up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Companies can also tap into the Water Efficiency Fund to install water-saving devices to mitigate over the longer run price increases.

sections.label: Su Xian accounts officer job
sections.summary: Su Xian eventually found a position as an accounts officer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Su Xian eventually found a position as an accounts officer.

sections.label: YCN fees and accessibility
sections.summary: The YCN has no fees and is not limited to any Institute of Higher Learning, so it is accessible to all.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: With no fees and not limited to any Institute of Higher Learning, the YCN is accessible to all.

sections.label: National Talent Bank proposal
sections.summary: A National Talent Bank is needed where jobseekers and would-be jobseekers can access conveniently to be headhunted for jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Going forward, we would need a National Talent Bank where jobseekers and would-be jobseekers can access conveniently, to be headhunted for jobs.

sections.label: NTUC U Family poll findings
sections.summary: An NTUC U Family online poll of 564 stay-at-home women planning to return to work reported ages, qualifications and intended work timelines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: A recent small-scale online poll by NTUC U Family done on stay-at-home women who plan to get back to work revealed that out of 564 female respondents, 94% are between the age of 25 and 54 years old which is in the prime working age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Of those in this age group, a significant majority, 73%, are Diploma and Degree holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: More than 60% of them intend to work within the year, while others, 20% or more, wish to do so within the next one to two years.

sections.label: Programme for re-joining women
sections.summary: The programme targets women looking to re-join the workforce and for employers to offer them a two to four months paid trial period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The programme targets women who are looking to re-join the workforce, and for employers to offer them a two to four months paid trial period.

sections.label: HDB flat cost changes
sections.summary: Families in 1- and 2-room HDB flats will on average see no net increases, and typical 4-room flat families a $5 extra on average.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Families in 1- and 2-room HDB flats will, on average, see no net increases, and families living in a typical 4-room HDB flat will see a $5 extra on average.

sections.label: Water tariff increase for stalls
sections.summary: The new water tariff raises each stall's costs by around $30 a month, and three in four businesses face an increase of less than $25 a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With the new water tariff, each stall will see an increase of around $30 a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, while there is an increase, it is unclear that it will lead to a significant increase in the cost of living.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am also relieved to hear that three in four businesses will see an increase of less than $25 a month, which also addresses Mr Dennis Tan's concern.

sections.label: National coordinating body for CFE
sections.summary: A strong national coordinating body is needed to implement the decade-long CFE strategy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To implement our decade-long CFE strategy, we will be well served by a strong national coordinating body.

sections.label: Starting CFE transformation quickly
sections.summary: The CFE transformation must start quickly, with ITMs rolled out far earlier than the proposed end-of-financial-year deadline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My third point about the CFE is that we must start our transformation quickly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We should roll out our ITMs as quickly as we can, far earlier than the proposed deadline of end of this financial year.

sections.label: Resources set aside for CFE
sections.summary: Close to $7 billion is set aside for the whole CFE, including $4.5 billion for the Industry Transformation Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In fact, I am heartened to hear that considerable resources are set aside for our industries − close to $7 billion for the whole CFE, including $4.5 billion for the Industry Transformation Programme.

sections.label: Micro-jobs for seniors
sections.summary: This is done by creating micro-jobs for seniors in social services, creating a national digital platform and app, and equipping seniors through SkillsFuture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: By doing three things: one, creating micro-jobs for our seniors starting with those in the social services; two, creating a national digital platform and app; and three, equipping our seniors to do these micro-jobs through SkillsFuture.

sections.label: Government spearheading gig economy
sections.summary: Seniors cannot do it alone, so the Government must spearhead a gig economy for seniors, starting with social services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But they also confide that they cannot do it alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: That is why we need the Government to spearhead a gig economy for our seniors, using social services as a start.

sections.label: Digital initiative and internationalisation funds
sections.summary: The passage calls for a national digital initiative for seniors and notes Budget measures including a $600 million International Partnership Fund and a proposed Global Innovation Alliance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And it can help reduce our social spending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Therefore, I call for the creation of a national digital initiative for our seniors involving our social services Ministries, VWOs and SkillsFuture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It will take a few years to get this done, so I hope we can start soon.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: The new Budget introduces a $600 million International Partnership Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: It also extends the existing Internationalisation Finance Scheme which has worked very well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: Under this strategy, the Committee suggests the setting up a Global Innovation Alliance, linking our institutes of higher learning to the leading innovation hubs in the world.

sections.label: Trump withdraws from TPP
sections.summary: President Trump signed an executive order to withdraw from the Trans-Pacific Partnership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: Amongst the first executive orders President Trump signed was to withdraw from the Trans-Pacific Partnership.

sections.label: 30% water price hike
sections.summary: The passage states the 30% hike is a necessary and small insurance compared to billions needed for future water plants and pipeline infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: The belated 30% hike, put in context, is a necessary and small insurance compared to the billions of dollars we need to set aside for future new water plants and pipeline infrastructure.

sections.label: Funding for overseas internships
sections.summary: The CFE outlined the Government's intention to provide more funding to support overseas internships and work attachments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: The CFE also outlined the Government's intention to provide more funding to support overseas internships and work attachments.

sections.label: China cashless payments comparison
sections.summary: The passage cites Alibaba's Single's Day sales and WeChat Pay's use in China, and questions Singapore's struggle with non-standardised payment terminals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: Consider this, the Single's Day Sales on Alibaba amounted to S$25 billion sale in just one day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: That is 70% of all retails sales in Singapore for one year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: Still in China, WeChat Pay has become the de-facto cashless payment means in China, regardless of transaction amount and IT infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: By this, I mean, even hawkers at the wet market can take payment using WeChat Pay, without the cashless terminal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: It makes us wonder why we are still struggling with different non-standardised payment terminals in Singapore after many years of trying to go cashless.

sections.label: SkillsFuture and ITM funding
sections.summary: The passage states SkillsFuture and the ITMs are key pillars, with $1.5 billion and $4.5 billion set aside, and Budget 2017 focusing on on-the-job skills utilisation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: SkillsFuture and the ITMs are two key pillars of our strategy to help individuals and firms meet the challenges in the new economy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: And huge sums of money have been set aside for them − $1.5 billion in Budget 2015 to support SkillsFuture, not a small sum and more will be put in.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: And $4.5 billion for the ITMs in Budget 2016 and Budget 2017 announced further top-ups to this initiative to transform our industries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For SkillsFuture, Budget 2017 focuses on "on-the-job skills utilisation" to ensure a better match between training and jobs.

sections.label: Budget surplus and revenue sources
sections.summary: The FY 2016 Budget surplus was $5.18 billion, 50% larger than estimated, with higher 2017 expenditure and NIRC as the largest revenue source.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Budget surplus of $5.18 billion for FY 2016, 50% larger than originally estimated puts us in a better position to react to external shocks and potentially fund future needs in the remainder of the Government's term.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The reasons provided for why total expenditure budgeted for in 2017 increased by 5.2% over 2016 when revenues are only increasing at 1.1% are that they are mainly due to higher expenditures on public housing, higher development expenditures for water-related treatment and health expenditure arising from growth in patient subsidies and improved training and retention of healthcare workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Further, while the net investment returns contribution has helped turn our Budget into an overall surplus, the scale of its contribution relative to other sources of revenue is large, at 20% of our total revenue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It is the largest source of funds for our Budget, larger than corporate tax contributions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In a recent article on Bloomberg, Norway's Central Bank Chief warned of how the risk of a 50% decline in 10 years of their sovereign wealth fund increases five times if government withdrawals from the fund increases from 3% to 4% of the fund.

sections.label: Budget 2017 revenue diversification
sections.summary: Budget 2017 attempts to diversify revenue sources through a carbon tax, diesel tax restructuring and water price changes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In Budget 2017, we see attempts to diversify revenue sources − a carbon tax to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by large direct emitters such as power stations, the restructuring of diesel taxes and water price changes.

sections.label: NIRC share of operating revenue
sections.summary: NIRC has helped turn the budget into an overall surplus, contributing a 20% share of operating revenue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: With regard to Government revenue, NIRC has helped turn our budget into an overall surplus, contributing a 20% share of the operating revenue.

sections.label: CPF and tax for freelancers
sections.summary: The speaker suggests including the new economic model into the CPF and tax regime as more people freelance or join the shared economy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As more individuals are participating in the shared economy or becoming a freelancer, if a company who systematically engage individuals to work for them do not pay CPF or taxes, one leg of the equation in our social safety network will be missing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Hence, I suggest that we include the new economic model into our CPF and tax regime.
